channel.title: Stimpunks.World — what changed on the street
channel.description: Every change to the rooms, the street that joins them and the campground past the treeline, newest first — including the things that are not built yet. Generated from changelog.html by tools/make-feed.py, so the page and the feed cannot disagree.

item.title: The Office and Tasks have channels under Staff
item.description: The chat lists Tasks and the Office under Staff, at Ryan’s ask, beside the Town Hall’s private rooms. Each is a room on the CB whose channel, call and Be seen here are for the people who can open the page: our directors, board members and administrators. Until now anybody signed on could tune to either one’s channel, and both sat under Paperwork.

item.title: Three more channels in The Open Notebook
item.description: The monthly log has three more channels, at Ryan’s ask: The Desk Standard, The Goulet Pen Company and Doodlewithrachel, at the end of his list. Their last month of videos and shorts is in it now, and it refills with the rest every morning. All three are credited in the liner notes.

item.title: Every profile has a page of its own, and its owner chooses who may open it
item.description: Helen Edgar asked how to share her profile outside the street, so every profile now has a page of its own, at profile.html# and the username, with a link to it under the card in every profile on the radio and a Copy the link button on the page. Who can open your card is a new choice on your card, and it starts where every card already was: The community, anybody signed on to the CB. Only me keeps your card to yourself, takes your nameplate off Who’s online and takes you out of the community directory. Anybody with the link opens your page to people who are not on the CB. This changes “whatever is filled in is shown to anybody signed on, with no switch”, which was Ryan’s call of 2026-10-17; this one is Ryan’s too. A public page never shows props, a chat status or a way to message anybody; those stay on the radio, for people signed on, who get Props for and Message buttons on the page that open them there. Somebody signed off is told the same thing for every name it will not show, so the page cannot tell anybody which usernames exist, and no search engine lists a profile. Every customization is on the page, the nameplate included, and its animations move at MAX GLITTER, or at any setting after Let it move on the card, because Ryan said they are a big part of what people want to show off. What it shows and keeps. Changed: profile.html, profile-page.js, profile-page.css, cb.js, cb.css, netlify/cb/lib.mjs, netlify/functions/cb-profile-page.mjs, cb-profile-of.mjs, privacy.html, cb-guide.html and tools/make-profile.py, which holds all of it.

item.title: Real crystals round the Alchemist’s Arch
item.description: At Helen Edgar’s ask, every crystal on the Crystal Wheel now hangs round the Alchemist’s Arch in the Faery Yurt, as the wheel’s own photographs in round frames of amber and amethyst, up one side of the doorway, over the top and down the other. Each one is a way to its card in Myths & Legends, and every photograph is credited under the arch with its photographer and licence, as the cards credit them. They are still at every setting. Changed: faery-yurt.html, love.css (§14) and tools/make-yurt-myths.py, which writes them from the wheel’s data so the arch and the wheel cannot disagree.

item.title: A pouch to fill under the Crystal Wheel, and the arch at the top of the yurt
item.description: At Helen Edgar’s ask, a pouch to fill under the Crystal Wheel: put in up to three crystals, draw the string, and it says what is in it and a possible outcome, made of what each crystal brings out of its own belief or lore, from a clear head to a steady seat on a horse. It sends nothing and keeps nothing. The cauldron now says what you mixed and a possible outcome every time, made of what each herb brings out of its own story, as well as the brew’s name when it is in the book. Both say once, plainly, that an outcome is a story and never a promise, and tools/make-yurt-myths.py refuses a herb or a crystal that brings anything about a body. The Alchemist’s Arch is first in the Faery Yurt now, straight after the dial, before the Soundtrack, the Bookshelf and the Cinema, at Helen’s ask. Changed: faery-yurt.html, faery-myths-room.html, crystal-pouch.js, herb-basket.js, love.css (§128), data/yurt-myths.json and tools/make-yurt-myths.py.

item.title: The Herbery, a herb basket and a cauldron
item.description: At Helen Edgar’s ask, the Herbery, in Myths & Legends after the Crystal Wheel: rosemary, thyme, mint, basil, bay, lavender, rose, elder, yarrow and hawthorn, each drawn, with what it is and its myth or folklore, every line with its source. The yurt says so beside the Alchemist’s Arch. Gather it, signed on to the CB, puts a herb in your herb basket in Profile on the radio, drawn as a wicker basket with the herbs standing in it, with Put it back beside each and the brews and stews it could make. It is the crystal pouch’s arrangement: which herbs and nothing about when, nothing counted, Show my herb basket on the CB off until switched on, and Forget me empties it. The privacy page said so first. The cauldron takes two or three herbs and names the brew or stew you stirred from the room’s own book, or tells you it is yours to name. It sends nothing and keeps nothing. The brews and stews are stories made of words, never recipes, and the room says nothing in it is to eat or drink; tools/make-yurt-myths.py refuses a measure or a dose in the Herbery. Changed: faery-myths-room.html, faery-yurt.html, herb-basket.js (new), netlify/cb/lib.mjs, netlify/cb/lib.test.mjs, netlify/functions/cb-herbs.mjs and cb-herbs-of.mjs (new), netlify/functions/cb-pets.mjs, cb.js, love.css (the herbs’ inks in §2, the Herbery in §128), privacy.html, data/yurt-myths.json, tools/make-yurt-myths.py and tools/check-contrast.py.

item.title: A crystal pouch, and the Green Witch’s shelf
item.description: At Helen Edgar’s ask, every card on the Crystal Wheel has Take it with you, signed on to the CB, and the crystal goes into your crystal pouch, in Profile on the radio, drawn as a medieval leather pouch with a drawstring tied in a bow and your crystals spilled onto a cloth at its foot, at Helen’s ask; under it, a small drawing of each stone in its own colours, never anybody’s photograph, each linked back to its card, and Put it back beside it. Show my crystal pouch on the CB, off until switched on and only for a claimed username, puts a Crystals tab in your profile. The pouch keeps which crystals and nothing about when, nothing counts who has which, and Forget me and deleting the username empty it. The privacy page said so before the pouch was built. The Green Witch’s Shelf, in Myths & Legends: Arin Murphy-Hiscock’s Green Witch books, each linked to its own page at its publisher, Simon & Schuster UK, and never to Amazon, which tools/make-yurt-myths.py now refuses. The Green Witch’s Book of Seasons says the day it is out. Changed: faery-myths-room.html, crystal-pouch.js (new), netlify/cb/lib.mjs, netlify/cb/lib.test.mjs, netlify/functions/cb-crystals.mjs and cb-crystals-of.mjs (new), netlify/functions/cb-pets.mjs, cb.js, love.css (the pouch’s inks in §2, the button in §128), privacy.html, data/yurt-myths.json, tools/make-yurt-myths.py and tools/check-contrast.py.

item.title: The Crystal Wheel, in Myths & Legends
item.description: At Helen Edgar’s ask, a Crystal Wheel in Myths & Legends, behind her yurt: photographs of popular crystals round a circle, each one pressed to its card, with what the stone really is, the belief or story attached to it and whether that is old tradition or modern crystal lore, and its birthstone month where it has one. The yurt says so beside the Alchemist’s Arch. The photographs are other people’s, from Wikimedia Commons, each credited on its card with its licence, as those licences ask, and listed in the liner notes. tools/make-yurt-myths.py now refuses a crystal photograph without its photographer, its Commons page or a licence this site can use, and one still carrying camera data. The wheel says once, with its source, that the meanings are not medicine. Changed: faery-myths-room.html, faery-yurt.html, love.css (§128 and §14), data/yurt-myths.json, tools/make-yurt-myths.py, liner-notes.html, and the photographs in crystals/.

item.title: The forums are sealed where they are kept
item.description: Every forum topic, every category’s list of topics, and every picture and file posted or waiting to be posted are now encrypted where they are kept at Netlify, with the same key of their own as Tasks. Ryan asked for the staff categories; every category is sealed, because a topic moved out of a staff category keeps the name it is stored under and must never be left in the clear. It is not end-to-end: our server opens them for whoever may read the category. Without the key the forums are shut rather than written in the clear. The privacy page says so. Changed: netlify/cb/lib.mjs, the forums’ two functions, privacy.html, and tools/make-forum.py, which now refuses anything of the forums written in the clear.

item.title: Tasks are sealed where they are kept
item.description: Every task, its comments, its activity, everybody’s Tasks notifications and saved filters, the recurring tasks and the templates are now encrypted where they are kept at Netlify, with a key of their own that neither the office nor direct messages use. Ryan’s call, after direct messages; the staff forum categories come next. It is done by the store itself for every name on its list, so nothing in Tasks had to change to be sealed. It is not end-to-end: our server opens them for whoever may read Tasks. Without the key Tasks are shut rather than written in the clear. The privacy page says so. Changed: netlify/cb/lib.mjs, the Tasks and hourly functions, privacy.html, and tools/make-tasks.py, which now refuses anything of Tasks written in the clear.

item.title: Direct messages are sealed where they are kept
item.description: Every conversation in Messages, every picture sent in one, your switch and your blocks, and any report copied from them are now encrypted where they are kept at Netlify, with a key of their own that nothing else on the street uses. Ryan’s call. Somebody who got at the stored files alone could not read them. It is still not end-to-end: our server opens them to show the two of you your conversation, and a report to our moderators. Without the key, Messages is shut rather than written in the clear. The privacy page says so. Changed: netlify/cb/lib.mjs, the three Messages functions, cb.js, privacy.html, cb-guide.html, and tools/check-messages.py, which now refuses anything of a conversation written in the clear.

item.title: Every channel says what it keeps, and the desk sets it
item.description: A channel now keeps its latest hundred messages, each for two weeks, unless our administrators set it otherwise at the desk in the Moderators’ room: World, any room’s channel, every channel at once, or direct messages, each from 50 to 1,000 messages and from a day to a year, or for good. Ryan’s call, after requests for more to scroll back through. The privacy page was rewritten first. A longer time never reaches what was already said. Every message is marked, when it is sent, with how long its channel kept messages then, and it is never kept longer than that. A shorter time, or fewer messages, reaches everything at once. The one exception is Pets, whose two writers, Ryan and Norah, both said yes to what they had already said there being kept as long as the channel now keeps it. The radio says what the channel you are on keeps, first under In this channel, and shows the latest hundred messages, with Earlier messages above them for a hundred more each time. It now asks the channel only for what has changed, so a long channel costs no more to listen to than a short one. The CB guide says how it works. Changed: netlify/cb/lib.mjs, netlify/functions/cb-channel.mjs, a new netlify/functions/cb-channel-rules.mjs, cb.js, cb.css, desk.js, town-hall-moderators.html, privacy.html, cb-guide.html, community-center.html, and the rooms that say how long a message stays.

item.title: The CB keeps a message for two weeks
item.description: Every message on the CB now stays two weeks from when it was sent, on World, in every room’s channel, between two people in Messages and on the Slake. Ryan’s call, after requests from our community for more to scroll back through, in channels like Pets above all; it was 48 hours. The privacy page was rewritten first. A message keeps the time it was sent under: anything sent on or before 2026-10-25, Colorado time, still goes at its 48 hours, and nothing is kept a minute longer for the change. A channel still holds fifty messages at most, so a busy one shows its latest fifty rather than a full two weeks. A time on the radio more than a week back says its date, because a day’s name could be either week. The forums’ Watering hole and Coping keep a topic a week after its last post, as they did. Changed: netlify/cb/lib.mjs, cb.js, world.js, forum.js, the rooms that say how long a message stays (Community Care, Coping, Pets, Show Your Work), privacy.html, cb-guide.html, community-center.html, forum.html and every other sentence that said 48 hours or two days.

item.title: Myths & Legends, through the Alchemist’s Arch in the Faery Yurt
item.description: A new room behind Helen Edgar’s yurt, at her ask: Myths & Legends, reached through the Alchemist’s Arch, an open stone arch set with amethyst crystals up both sides and amber stones round its curve, with the four elements carved in its keystone and dawn over a stone circle seen through it. At MAX GLITTER the amber glows and the amethyst glints, and at every other setting it stands still; the yurt’s dial line says so. Inside: Stonehenge, with a sun you turn between midsummer sunrise and midwinter sunset, and what is known about where its stones came from; King Arthur and Merlin, how the story grew from the 800s to Malory, and the places that claim him; the folk under the hill, from boggarts and hobs to Black Shuck and the Lambton Worm; story-or-fact cards you turn over; the Wheel of the Year; and a shelf of old books on fairies, myth and Arthur, every one free to read. It is the Reading Room’s house, lit through stone rather than by a flame. Every fact names the page it was read on, and tools/make-yurt-myths.py refuses one that does not, a story-or-fact card with only one side, and a book whose author or translator died less than seventy years ago. Where a source corrected the usual telling, the room follows the source: the midsummer sun rises just to the left of the Heel Stone, and the Altar Stone came from north-east Scotland. The Golden Bough carries a line saying its big theories have since been set aside. Four Tinker Bell films on Films I Love in the Cinema: The Great Fairy Rescue, Secret of the Wings, The Pirate Fairy and Legend of the NeverBeast, Disney UK’s own trailers. Changed: faery-myths-room.html, faery-yurt.html, love.css (§128, and Small screens and Print are now §129 and §130), data/yurt-myths.json, data/yurt-cinema.json, and the street’s lists: the sitemap, the map, the chat page’s tags, the fractal window, the Adventurer’s Guild (a piece of amber with a beetle in it) and a share card.

item.title: Labyrinth, The NeverEnding Story and Studio Ghibli in the Cinema
item.description: Ten more reels on Films I Love in the Cinema behind the Faery Yurt, at Helen Edgar’s ask: the trailers for The NeverEnding Story (1984), Labyrinth (1986), with David Bowie, and The Princess Bride (1987), from Rotten Tomatoes Classic Trailers like most of the shelf; Coraline (2009), from LAIKA, the studio that made it; and six of Studio Ghibli’s, from GKIDS Films, their distributor: Spirited Away, My Neighbor Totoro, Howl’s Moving Castle, Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind, The Secret World of Arrietty and Whisper of the Heart. Every one answered OK and can be played here on its watch page. Changed: data/yurt-cinema.json, faery-cinema-room.html, and the Cinema’s book in faery-yurt.html.

item.title: Your page, and every notification kept for 30 days
item.description: Notifications come and go, so the CB keeps them for you now. Ryan’s ask: Tasks kept its own notifications for 30 days, and nothing else did. Every notification one of your devices is sent is also kept for you, once however many of your devices it went to, for 30 days. It reverses what the privacy page said, that nothing about what was sent to a device is kept, and the page was rewritten first. It keeps no words: what kind it was and why, who from, where, which message, post, task, suggestion or event, and when. The words are read again each time you look, from wherever they still are and only where your username can still read them, so a message gone at its 48 hours, or taken off, is there only as that there was one. Only what a device was actually sent is kept, so what you switch on under Notifications decides it. Nobody else is shown it, a moderator included, and nothing counts it. Clear my past notifications, Forget me and deleting your username delete it. Your page is where they are: the radio’s You part docked into a page of its own, the way the chat page docks the radio, with Profile open, Past notifications beside it, and Unreads, Messages and Your radio after them. Your page under You on the radio goes there. Each past notification is said the way the notification said it, because the service worker’s wording is now one block the radio carries an identical copy of. The CB guide says how it works. Changed: netlify/cb/lib.mjs, netlify/functions/cb-notices.mjs, cb.js, cb-sw.js, cb.css, you.html, privacy.html, cb-guide.html, and a new checker, tools/check-notices.py.

item.title: Adding somebody to our mailing lists says it worked
item.description: Pressing Add them to Givebutter’s lists in the office now answers with what happened: that Givebutter has them on those lists, and whether they were in Givebutter already, as somebody added there by hand is, or Givebutter made a new contact for them. Until now the panel was drawn again with a line about taking people off lists at its foot, which read as the answer to adding them. That line is kept for a later visit to the join request, where it says the office cannot take them off. The office learns whether they were there already from when Givebutter says it made their contact, and keeps nothing of Givebutter’s answer; the privacy page says so. Changed: netlify/cb/lib.mjs, office.js and privacy.html.

item.title: Join requests reach our mailing lists, now for real
item.description: The reason Givebutter refused was the email address, not a name. The entry below gave one name as the likeliest reason, and it was not: with Givebutter now saying why, it answered “The emails.0 must be an array.” Givebutter’s API reference lists a contact’s emails as plain addresses, and its server wants each one as an object, so Add them to Givebutter’s lists had failed on every press since it arrived on 2026-10-23. The office sends the address as Givebutter’s primary email now, a plain address, which its reference and its server agree on. What is sent is unchanged: their email address, their first and last name when they have both, and the lists they said yes to. Changed: netlify/cb/lib.mjs.

item.title: Mailing lists for somebody with one name
item.description: Adding somebody from a join request to our mailing lists failed with “Givebutter did not take it (it answered 422)”. The likeliest reason: the office sent Givebutter whatever name their contact had, and a one-word name on the Join form is filed as a last name with no first. Givebutter keeps a contact by a first and a last name together, or by an email address with no name, so the office now sends the two names together or neither, and somebody with one name goes to Givebutter by their email address alone, which the office says when it happens. Their name can be added in Givebutter. The privacy page says so too. Changed: netlify/cb/lib.mjs, office.js and privacy.html. When Givebutter refuses, the office now says why, in Givebutter’s own words, beside the number, to the director who pressed, so a refusal for any other reason says what it is. Nothing of it is kept.

item.title: The Sandbox opens on its title
item.description: In The Sandbox, the dial comes after the room’s title now, under the laptop and centred on it, where it had stood first on the page and to the left. Every other room puts its title first. Ryan’s ask. The dial stands where the room’s artifact put its preview dial, so the copy the street imports was changed to put it under the laptop, and it was brought in again; nothing else in the room changed. Changed: sandbox.html, love.css and data/rooms/sandbox.json. Bringing a room in again kept rewriting the date the liner notes say it arrived on the street. It keeps the day it first arrived now. Changed: tools/import-room.py.

item.title: Notifications from the suggestion box
item.description: Two new switches under Notifications in Your radio on the CB, each off until you switch it on. When a moderator replies to a suggestion of mine tells you when a moderator replies to something you dropped in The Sandbox’s suggestion box, and whether they marked it done, not doing or open again. Something new in the suggestion box, offered only to our moderators, tells them when a suggestion is dropped in, or when whoever dropped it in replies, so whichever of them switch it on know without watching the box. Until now nobody was told about a new suggestion at all. Pressing the notification opens the box on that suggestion. Ryan’s ask, and Norah’s. Everything, and anything added later takes both in, as it says. A notification says who did it and what, and, unless you switched the words off, the suggestion’s title and the first words of what they wrote. It never says how many are waiting, and nobody is told about what they wrote themselves. Changed: cb.js, cb-sw.js, sandbox.html, privacy.html, data/sandbox.json, netlify/cb/lib.mjs and netlify/functions/cb-suggest.mjs.

item.title: Replies and Me too in the suggestion box
item.description: Every suggestion in The Sandbox’s suggestion box has a thread of replies now, from our moderators and from whoever dropped it in, as many as it takes, each with its username, its date and pictures if you like. A moderator’s reply can mark it done, not doing, or open again, and where it stands is always the newest reply that marked it, so taking that reply down takes its mark with it. Whoever wrote a reply can edit it, and they or a moderator can take it down. The one answer a suggestion had before is its first reply. This replaces the reply that left a suggestion open, from earlier the same morning. Ryan’s ask. Me too says a suggestion affects you too. Anybody signed on can press it on somebody else’s suggestion and press it again to take it back. It is not a vote: the box names who a suggestion affects, alphabetically, and never says how many, the CB’s rule for a reaction, and nothing is sorted by it. Ryan’s ask, to keep the box away from upvoting. Changed: suggest.js, love.css, sandbox.html, privacy.html, community-center.html, data/sandbox.json, data/community.json, netlify/cb/lib.mjs, netlify/functions/cb-suggest.mjs and tools/make-sandbox.py.

item.title: A moderator can reply in the suggestion box and leave it open
item.description: In The Sandbox’s suggestion box, a moderator’s reply can leave a suggestion open, to ask a question or say where it has got to, without marking it done or not doing. Choosing Still open used to throw away whatever the moderator wrote and take any answer off; now the reply stays on it, with its pictures, under Still open, a reply from and the moderator’s username, and it stays in the box’s Open filter. Still open with no reply still takes any answer off. Ryan’s ask. Changed: suggest.js, sandbox.html, privacy.html, data/sandbox.json, netlify/cb/lib.mjs and netlify/functions/cb-suggest.mjs.

item.title: Screenshots in the suggestion box
item.description: A suggestion, a feature request or a bug report in The Sandbox’s suggestion box can carry pictures now, up to four, a screenshot of a bug most of all, and so can a moderator’s answer. Add one with Add a picture, or paste or drop one into the words. This reverses the box’s words only, which it had because a screenshot is a picture of somebody’s screen: Ryan’s call, written into the privacy page first. Each picture is redrawn in your browser before it goes, by the CB’s own redraw, which takes off everything a camera or a phone wrote into it; each needs a sentence saying what it shows; and the form asks you to tick that you have looked at all of it and it shows nothing private, because a picture in the box is as public as its words. A picture is shown only while the box holds it, and goes with the suggestion, or with the answer that lets go of it. Changed: suggest.js, love.css, sandbox.html, privacy.html, community-center.html, data/sandbox.json, data/community.json, netlify/cb/lib.mjs, netlify/functions/cb-suggest-image.mjs, netlify/functions/cb-midnight.mjs and tools/make-sandbox.py. The box’s line for somebody not signed on said you are given the starter password when you join our community. It says you join with an invite and a username of your own, as everywhere else since 2026-10-21.

item.title: Bring another animal to Chimera Obscura’s bench
item.description: In Chimera Obscura, the animals are filed by class: mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, fish and invertebrates, each class alphabetical, in every animal picker on the bench and in the list of what is on the shelf at the foot of the page. A picker still jumps to an animal when you type its first letter. Bring another animal takes the place of Let any part come from any animal, which put every animal on the shelf under every part. The bench starts with two animals; each press brings one more, with a picker of its own, up to one for every part, and every part’s choices are only the animals on the bench, so they stay one press each however long the shelf gets. The button under each picker after the second takes that animal off again, and the parts that came from it go to the first animal. A chimera opened from a link puts every animal it was made from on the bench. Ryan’s call. Changed: chimera-obscura.html, chimera-obscura.js, chimera.js, love.css, data/chimera-obscura.json and tools/make-chimera-obscura.py.

item.title: Choosing a body on the bench keeps everything else
item.description: In Chimera Obscura, choosing the second animal’s body changes the body and nothing else. It used to make the second animal the first one too, so both selectors named the same animal, the second one dropped out of every part, and every part chosen so far went back to it. Reported by our community. Changing the first or second animal now changes only the parts that came from the animal it replaces. A part chosen from the other animal, the body included, stays where it was put. Changed: chimera-obscura.js.

item.title: A bat, a crow, a meerkat, a lion, a tiger, a rhino, a camel and a hippo on Chimera Obscura’s shelf
item.description: New on the shelf in Chimera Obscura, from Ryan’s list: a bat, a crow, a meerkat, a lion, a tiger, a rhino, a camel and a hippo. The zebra on the list was already there. Every part of each goes with every part of every other animal, as before. They brought parts nothing on the shelf had, and each goes on any animal: a lion’s mane and a camel’s humps under Back; a bat’s wings both ways, spread under Back and folded down its sides under Arms; a rhino’s horns on the nose; a camel’s eyelashes; a bat’s fangs and a hippo’s tusks; and among the markings a tiger’s stripes, a rhino’s folds and a crow’s blue gloss. A lion with a tiger’s parts is suggested as a Liger and a tiger with a lion’s as a Tigon, the names English already has for the two together. A crow before an animal whose name starts with a vowel is a Cro, so a crow with an opossum’s parts is a Croopossum: the room checks every name it can suggest, and the plain join had a slur in the middle of it. Every list of animals is in alphabetical order now: the first and second animal, every part’s choices, and the list of what is on the shelf at the foot of the page. Changed: chimera.js, data/chimera-obscura.json and tools/make-chimera-obscura.py.

item.title: A call’s window has the radio’s grip and its − and +
item.description: A room’s call moves and sizes the way the radio does. Move is the six dots, and Small and Large are − and +, which go one size at a time between Large, the whole window, Regular, where a call opens, Small, a tile in the corner, and Stamp, which is new: the size of a postage stamp, the picture and the bar and nothing else. Each says which size it goes to, and says so when the call is already as small or as large as it goes. The call carries on through every change. The CB guide has the rest.

item.title: Symphrenia Chill in the Music Room
item.description: A third playlist on Helen’s phonograph, at her ask: the Music Room plays Symphrenia Chill, Zbigniew Preisner, Brian Eno, Philip Glass and Erik Satie, whole or a record at a time off a shelf of its own, and the yurt has a songbook of it like the others. Its shelf opens with something to read alongside it: Existential Diversity, the Symphrenic Bodymind and Wider Existence, by Helen Edgar and David Gray-Hammond, on The Wider Existence. Any of her playlists can carry a link like that now, with the writers named beside it. Every playlist in her rooms was read again the same day. Strange things will happen has two more songs on its shelf, Big Thief’s “Velvet Ring” and a mix of songs like it, which she had added since; the others had not changed.

item.title: The Reading Room points at where you can borrow a book
item.description: Helen’s Reading Room now says where to borrow a book, at her ask: its spines open their authors’ pages, and a line under the bookcases’ introduction sends anybody who wants the book itself across the campgrounds to Ryan’s shelves in the cave at the Solarpunk Hermitage, where every book has a link to borrow it or read it.

item.title: Back to the street puts you where you were on it
item.description: A room’s way back takes you back to where you were, not to the top of the page. “Back to the street” opens the street at the door you went in by, “back through the leaves” opens the Jungle Room at the door to the Den, and the same goes for every room’s way back to the street, to the room in front of it, or to its area: the Campgrounds, the Outskirts, the caverns and the rest. It is what your browser’s own Back button does, and the forums, tasks and the office have done it since 2026-10-21. From a room behind a room it goes back more than one step, and Forward walks you in again. It keeps nothing. It uses your browser’s own history for this tab, and nothing is stored or sent for it. If you came into a room from somewhere else, so this tab has never been where the link goes, the link goes there the ordinary way, to the top. A link to one part of the street still goes to that part, and a door into a room still opens it at its top. It reaches every room, the ways back from the Faery Yurt’s own rooms into the yurt included, as the street’s conventions do.

item.title: A link to any section, from the # beside its heading
item.description: Every section heading on the street has a # beside it now, in the heading’s own ink and lettering. Pressing it copies a link straight to that section, to send somebody to the part of a room or a document that matters. It says “Link copied” beside it, and to a screen reader. On a computer it shows when you point at the heading or reach it with the keyboard; on a phone or tablet it is always there, because nothing there can point. A link to a section lasts. Each heading got its name in the address once, from its words, and keeps it if the heading is reworded later, so a link already sent still lands. In the forums, a heading in a post has a # too, so a Wiki or Team Docs page can be linked to one section of it. The link opens the topic at that heading. It names the heading by a short code rather than its words, as the forums’ links name topics and posts by theirs. Swaying Sweetgrass’s sign-off had been sitting just under the meadow’s header, with the rest of the room after it, because the page closed its main part early. The whole meadow is inside it now, and the sign-off is at the foot.

item.title: Unreads is at the top of the chat page
item.description: On the chat page, Unreads is above the channels now, at the top of the left-hand column, instead of under every channel, where reaching it took a lot of scrolling. On a narrow screen it comes just before the button that opens the channels, so the channel itself is no further down than it was. The radio on every other page is as it was, with Unreads under Who’s around. The CB guide says where it is on each.

item.title: Anybody signed on walks straight into Cavendish’s open meetings
item.description: The lobby is for guests now. In the calls in the Events Room, the Operations Room and the Editorial Room, anybody signed on to the CB comes straight in, and only somebody joining without an account knocks and waits. You come in as one of the call’s moderators, because 8x8 lets nobody else past its lobby. So anybody signed on in those three calls can let a guest in, and can also mute or remove people, end the meeting for everybody and switch the lobby off. This changes our earlier rule that the base station is the only moderator, for those three calls only; every other room’s call is as it was, and recording and transcription are still the base station’s alone. Each room’s call panel, Cavendish Coworking and the privacy page say so.

item.title: A room’s page can be named on the CB, as well as its channel
item.description: Type / and the start of a room’s name in the message box and the radio offers the rooms’ pages, the way # offers rooms. The message carries /the-den, and every radio shows it as /The Den, linked to the room’s page. On the chat page a #the-den opens The Den’s channel there, so /the-den is how to send somebody to the room itself. Anywhere else both go to the room, as a #tag always has. Only a room is a link: a / after a space or at the start of a line, in lower case, naming a room on the street. and/or, /usr/bin and /the-den/somewhere stay words. The CB guide says so. The teleporter shows each room as /the-den now, on the radio and on the guest bar, because it takes you to the room’s page. Typing #the-den or /the-den into it still finds The Den.

item.title: The Adventurer’s Guild reads in a low-stimulation mode again
item.description: The Adventurer’s Guild went blank in every low-stimulation mode, since the modes arrived this morning. A mode gives every box on a page its quiet ground, and the layer the guild’s fanfare throws its sparks into covers the whole window, see-through until a fanfare, so the mode turned it into a sheet over every word. Decoration takes no ground in a mode now, so it stays see-through. The same fix brought back words in other rooms that were partly hidden in a mode: the keys on the Playhouse’s sound board, lines under the pool of light in the Healing Checkpoint, and lines under a vine, the notebook’s highlighter and the pebble stones in the Faery Yurt. Maintenance in the Faery Yurt, which changes nothing you can see outside a mode: its two vines are marked as decoration, as the drawings inside them already were, and its shutters are marked as covering their windows on purpose, so in a mode they stay shut rather than turning see-through. The check that Gentle never takes away the words now renders every page in a mode as well, and stops the build if anything the mode filled in lies over a word.

item.title: The low-stimulation modes are CB themes too
item.description: A new group under the radio’s Themes: Low stimulation, by request: Warm Light, Cool Dark, Plant Green and Red Light, the dial’s four modes, for the radio alone. The room keeps its own colours and only the radio goes quiet. Each is the radio exactly as it is in that mode, the same colours by name, with no drawing and nothing that moves, and every word clears 4.5 to 1. The dial’s modes still lay one over the whole page. The CB guide has them. They are themes everywhere the CB’s themes are: for the call window, for your profile card, and for the forums when you give them a theme of their own. The CB guide’s paragraph on the Glitter dial reads properly again: a sentence about the radio’s own window had been pasted into itself.

item.title: Video cards play even when their length is not known
item.description: A YouTube or Vimeo card on the CB, or a video preview in the forums, plays now even when our server could not find out how long the video runs, Ryan’s call: the player shows its length the moment it starts. Its button says the length when it is known. So YouTube links on the live site play, key or no key. Only a video that cannot play on other sites is a link to YouTube instead: one its maker keeps off other sites, an age-restricted one, one not yet live, or a private one. The rooms’ own play buttons all still say how long they run, and four sentences that spoke for every button on the street now speak for the rooms’: in the Adventurer’s Guild, Big Steep Fermentables, Breaker Breaker and Swaying Sweetgrass.

item.title: YouTube cards ask YouTube how long a video runs
item.description: On the live site, YouTube links on the CB were coming out as links to YouTube rather than players. A card plays a video only when it can say how long it runs, and from our host’s servers YouTube’s pages would not say. Our server can now ask YouTube’s own Data API instead, sending it only the video’s id, and YouTube cards play once that is switched on. The forums’ previews ask it too. An age-restricted video, one not yet live and one its maker keeps off other sites stay links to YouTube.

item.title: Links on the CB become cards, and videos play in them
item.description: A link in a message on the CB gets a card a moment after the message goes out, by request: the site’s name, who made it, its title as a link that says where it goes, and its description, or for a post on X or Bluesky the words of the post. Up to three in a message. A YouTube or Vimeo video plays right in the card, behind a press that says how long it runs. Nothing from YouTube or Vimeo loads until somebody presses it. Our server reads each link once, just after the message goes out, so the site sees our host and never you or anybody reading. A card never has a picture, and nothing a site sends to put on a page is put on ours. Any site that publishes an oEmbed endpoint is read for its words; the ones that play here are the ones the street already plays. Write a link in angle brackets, <https://…>, to send it without a card. The CB guide and the privacy page have the rest. A link in the forums reads the same oEmbed answers, so a post on X or Bluesky there now shows its words.

item.title: My own order for the chat page’s channels
item.description: My own order is a fourth way to sort the channels under tags on the chat page, by request. Arrange puts Move up and Move down beside every channel, each group on its own; Alt and an arrow on a channel moves it too, and so does dragging. A line says where each one went. It follows you from one device to another, because it is kept on our server under your username: which channels, in which order, under which group, and nothing about when. Nobody else is shown it, and Forget me and deleting your username delete it. The privacy page says so, and the CB guide says how. Going back to A to Z takes the line about the last order away, which it had been leaving behind.

item.title: The chat page’s channels, A to Z or by activity
item.description: On the chat page, the channels under each tag are A to Z now, passing over a leading The, A or An, so The Den is with the Ds. Community and Staff keep their own order. Sort the channels under tags can put them in another order: Recently active, newest message first, or Most active, most messages in the last 48 hours first. They are sorted only when the page opens, when you choose an order and when you press Sort again, never as messages come in, so nothing moves while you are reaching for it. The server sends the order and never a time or a number, leaves out any room that keeps to itself or that you cannot go into, and does not count the bot that says The Feed’s and The Source’s arrivals. Your browser remembers the order you chose. The CB guide and the privacy page have the rest.

item.title: Bigger headings on the CB, and In this channel in parts
item.description: Every heading inside a part of the radio is bigger, on every page and on the chat page: People, Calls going now and Your chat status under Who’s around, the Themes groups, Profile’s sections and the rest. The parts’ own headings went up a size with them, so a part still reads above what is in it, and the room’s name under Where you are is still the largest words on the radio. On the chat page, the groups of channels down the left are bigger: Community, Direct messages, Staff, Music and every other. In this channel is in smaller parts now, each under its own heading: Seen here (Be seen here, and who else is seen), In this room’s call (Join this room’s call, and who is in it), Your familiar (Bring my familiar, or where to find one) and On now. A heading with nothing under it just now is not shown. The CB guide says what is where.

item.title: The Glitter dial and Open in Chat, on the CB
item.description: The dial is on the radio now, by request: Glitter dial, beside I need a bodymind break under Where you are, opens Gentle, Regular and MAX GLITTER and the low-stimulation modes, so you can turn the dial or escape into a mode from any page the radio is on, the pages with no dial of their own included. It is the same dial, not a second one: turn either and the other follows. From the radio’s own window it turns the page you came from. Open in Chat comes after it and takes you to the chat page with the room you are in picked, or World on a page that is not a room. The CB guide has both. The dial at the top of a page says what Gentle, Regular and MAX GLITTER do again. Its line under the buttons had been blank since 2026-09-21, when the Playhouse’s toys took the same name in the street’s script and silently replaced the dial’s words; only the low-stimulation modes’ lines, added this morning, were showing.

item.title: Pets: down on the floor with the animals
item.description: Pets is a shopfront on the street, between Coping and Show Your Work: the floor at the end of the day, a dog and a cat asleep on the rug and a rabbit by the skirting board, the light in the window going, and nobody switching the lamp on, because getting up would mean moving somebody. Nothing in it moves, at any setting. It says why co-regulating with an animal matters so much to so many Autistic people, and to everybody else: an animal wants no eye contact, no small talk and no mask, and being with one can be enough. Mammals settle one another, and the room quotes the lines on our own pages that say so, from our Co-regulation and Polyvagal Theory entries, with Helen Edgar on being with somebody and our Body Doubling and Glimmers entries, each credited to whoever wrote it. Every room on the street with animals in it has a pet flap there, set into the skirting board at the height of whoever uses it: the three shelters, Pekoe and Purrs, the Run, the Truck Stop’s treat truck, the sanctuary at All Needs Met and Chimera Obscura. A new pets room on the street gets one too. Its channel on the CB is under Community on the chat page, for your animals: pictures, stories, worries and questions, and the ones who are gone. It is not a vet, says nothing about what an animal will do for your health, ranks no animal above another and counts nobody’s.

item.title: Following a link no longer hangs up your call
item.description: While you are in a call, anything on the CB that would take you off the page opens in a new tab instead, and the radio says so: a room’s #tag or a link on the channel or in a conversation, a room on Who’s online or Unreads, a room on somebody’s profile, the teleporter and Take to the forums. Following a link used to leave the page, and a page that goes takes its call with it. Every other way off the page asks first while a call is up: a link in the room itself, Back, or closing the tab brings up your browser’s own Leave site?. With no call up, links take you there as they always have. The CB guide has the rest, and Pop out still takes a call with you from room to room.

item.title: The chat page has its channels again
item.description: For a while after the chat status went up, the chat page showed the chat status where its channels belong, and the channel would not load: the new part had been given the same name in the radio’s code as the chat page’s list of channels, and replaced it. The channels are back, the chat status is under Who’s around where it should be, and the street’s checks now refuse two parts of a script sharing a name. Not right now does not hold your notifications, the way Discord’s Do Not Disturb does: those stay with the notification switches, device by device, because somebody showing red may still want to hear a mention.

item.title: Your chat status: come say hi, people i know, not right now
item.description: The CB has a chat status, at the foot of Who’s around on the radio: whether you would like to be talked to, because somebody can be about and still not be chatty. It is one of the interaction badges, in the words and shapes of the Cavendish Space Project’s interaction cards, after the colour communication badges Autism Network International started at the first Autreat: come say hi, a green circle; people i know, a yellow triangle; not right now, a red square. People see it beside your name on Who’s online and on Also seen here, on your profile under your name, and at the top of a conversation with you under Messages, with what the badge asks, so it can be checked before anybody writes. Each badge is its shape and its words as well as its colour, and looks the same in every theme. It is a sign, not a lock: it stops nobody writing to you. It starts as none, nothing changes it but you (no idle, nothing that runs out), and we keep which badge and nothing about when. The CB guide says why the street did not copy Discord’s Online, Idle, Do Not Disturb and Invisible: Be seen here is already Online and Invisible. The privacy page has the rest.

item.title: Coping: the eye of the storm
item.description: Coping is a shopfront on the street, between Community Care and Show Your Work: three pages from our Regulation and Coping hub on stimpunks.org, Seeds of Cope, The Science of Cope and Cope Is Not an Insult, summarised in one room in our own words, with their lines quoted where they say it best. Small things to reach for right now, the cope map, the seeds, words you can borrow, why coping works, and why cope is not an insult. It is the eye of the storm: clear sky straight up, a wall of storm cloud all the way round, and the dry floor of the eye in the sun. The storm stays in plain sight, all the way round and at the edges of a wide window, because the difference between coping and denial is that the storm is still there. Nothing in the eye moves by itself at any setting, MAX GLITTER included. Doors stand on the floor of the eye, each opening onto a room on the street for coping, regulation or peer support, grouped by the moment you are in, after our page’s own way of not getting lost: overloaded, socially fried, spiraling, post-crash, and when it is the system and you want people. Its channel on the CB is under Community on the chat page, for talking about coping. Dead Tired Society’s channel is no longer in Community, so the two do not compete; it is still under Coping and Calm with the rest of the street’s rooms. Community Care names Coping next door. It is not clinical advice and not a crisis line, and says so before its first heading, with the crisis lines. Nothing in it is grit, a sneer, clinical, counted or cheerful at you, and nothing on the page keeps anything about you.

item.title: Community’s rooms are under their tags too
item.description: On the chat page, the rooms in Community are now also under their tags, as every other room is: Dead Tired Society and Community Care under Coping, the Cave and the Community Center under Calm, the house at Cavendish and its meeting rooms under Meetings, the rooms with something to watch under Videos, and Show Your Work under Make/build and Art. They stay in Community as well. The Town Hall’s private rooms and World are not under any tag: the private rooms are only ever listed for the people who can go in, and World is the whole street’s channel, first in Community.

item.title: Rooms have tags, and the chat is grouped by them
item.description: Rooms have tags now, saying what each is for: Music, Videos, Pets, Pubs and restaurants, Games, Calm, Coping, Homes and Make/build, and, so that every room has one that is true of it, Reading, Art, Outdoors, Areas, Meetings, News and notices, Forums and Paperwork. The rooms in Community and Staff keep their own groups. On the chat page, the channels after Community and Staff are grouped by those tags, in place of the one long list called World. A room with more than one tag is under each, so the Latibulum is in Music, Videos, Calm and Coping. The forums’ categories follow The forums, under Forums. Find a channel finds a tag too: type pets and the whole Pets group comes up. The CB guide says so. Music and Videos mean something to press and play, so a room tagged either is held to Now Playing, and a room on that bill is tagged one of them. A new room on the street needs its tags before the chat will build.

item.title: Breaker Breaker: CB radios, CB slang and the long haul
item.description: Breaker Breaker is a new shopfront on the street, between Show Your Work and Your Room, for the citizens band: the radios, the way people talk on them, where the band came from, and the truckers who kept their sets on. It has a channel of its own on the CB. It is lit the way a convoy is at night: every light in it is a marker lamp, which shows where the edge of a rig is and lights nothing round it, amber at the front and sides and red at the back, because those are the law’s colours. Across the top, the interstate from the driver’s seat, drawn lamp by lamp, with the radio on the dash on 19. Nothing blinks and nothing moves at any setting. Why it is called the citizens band, and why this street took the word: a band for anybody, with no exam to pass and, from 1983, no licence, where people chose their own names. And what this street’s CB took from it: handles, a channel everybody shares and one for every room, 19, the squelch, off being off, nothing kept for long, and BASE. Steve Silberman on amateur radio, from NeuroTribes, read on our page about written communication, beside that page’s own line on text as a medium neurodivergent people helped build because they needed it. The slang, from breaker to the back door, in our words from Wikipedia’s list. The parts of that list that name people unkindly are left off. On the rack, Dale Watson’s three Truckin’ Sessions records, every song on the back of its sleeve with its own button, and C. W. McCall’s Convoy, each from its makers’ own channel. Not a line of any song is on the page. A job for the Adventurer’s Guild: the microphone has come off its hook. Racing Sans One and Titillium Web join the faces.

item.title: Jellies on the bodymind break
item.description: The bodymind break has jellies beside the forest, at Helen Edgar’s ask: Monterey Bay Aquarium’s Live Jelly Cam, the one on our Watering Hole Hangs list that the Jungle Room carries too. It is live, so its button says it runs until you close it rather than how long; like any live camera it can show an empty tank or nothing at all. Nothing reaches YouTube until you press it, and closing the break stops it. And then the break is done, in Helen’s words, so it stays a quiet screen and does not end up as busy as the rooms.

item.title: Feeling overwhelmed? Escape to a low-stimulation mode
item.description: Four low-stimulation modes in the dial’s box, under the levels: Warm Light, Cool Dark, Plant Green and Red Light. Each lays a few quiet colours over every room on the street and over the CB’s themes, for when the street is too much even at Gentle. Each button wears its own mode, so you can see what it does before you press it. The bodymind break offers them too. Every room is its own world, and a mode is the one time they all look alike, because you asked. It is the dial’s own idea: how loud the street is belongs to you. The rooms are untouched; leave the mode and every one is as it was. The same rooms and the same words: a word on the mode’s ground in its ink, every link underlined, every edge the mode’s line, no glow, no gradient and no picture behind the words, and nothing moving, so a mode is Gentle as well. Drawings, games, videos and players keep their shapes in the mode’s one colour. Pictures keep their own colours, for the polaroid wall’s promise that we do not filter anybody. Red Light is red and nothing else. It is on before a page appears, so nobody in a mode is shown a room’s colours on the way in, and it stays on every page until you leave it: press the mode again, Back to the rooms’ own colours, or a level. It is kept in your own browser as love-low and sent nowhere (the privacy page).

item.title: I need a bodymind break, from the dial and the CB
item.description: A calm screen over whatever page you are on, from I need a bodymind break: in the How loud do you want it? box at the top of a page, under Where you are on the CB’s radio, and as Break on the radio’s bar while it is folded and on the CB bar for anybody not signed on. Helen Edgar’s idea, because the street is busy even at Gentle: somewhere that is just a blank, cool screen to regulate in, saying breathe, it will be okay. Ryan’s answer was Cavendish Space’s button of the same name, put in the CB, and then in the dial’s box too, which Helen said yes to. A far treeline in mist, and a few words: dusk on a device set dark, mist on one set light, with every word measured on both. Nothing on it moves, at any setting, MAX GLITTER included. For when a break is not enough (Helen’s ask the same day): crisis lines and warmlines and our Help page, as buttons, near the top, and, lower down, somewhere quiet on the street: Stay Frosty, the Healing Checkpoint or the Latibulum. A forest to watch, if you like, the one Helen linked: Forest 4K, a nature film by Relaxation Film with music by Richard Nomad, three hours of streams, birdsong and soft piano, which says how long it runs before you press it and fetches nothing from YouTube until you do. Back to the quiet screen puts it away, and closing the break stops it. It asks before it stops anything. If a film or a recording on the page is playing, the break says so and offers Pause it; it pauses nothing by itself, because somebody may have the Latibulum’s ocean waves on because they want them. While it is up the radio reads nothing aloud, and what was said meanwhile is on the channel when you come back. It keeps nothing and sends nothing, and its own script is not downloaded until the first press. The privacy page says so, and the CB guide says where the buttons are. I’m back, or Escape, closes it and puts you back where you were.

item.title: Show Your Work’s bench takes photographs, under the polaroid wall’s rules
item.description: A card on the bench can carry a photograph of the work, under the polaroid wall’s rules: the yes of whoever took it and anybody in it, a description of what is in it in its maker’s own words, nothing a camera writes into the file, and gone, not hidden, the moment its maker asks. Ryan’s call, the same evening the room opened with none. Every one is a record on the wall’s own list, kept off Enid’s wall and naming this room, so the tool that builds the wall walks the bench like every other page and refuses a photograph with no record, no description, camera data or a filter. Shown whole: not cropped, not filtered. Put yours on the bench and the Community Center’s service board say what to send.

item.title: Show Your Work, a garage with the door rolled up
item.description: Show Your Work is a shopfront on the street, between Community Care and Your Room: a garage with its door rolled up, where the work of folks in our community is shown before it is finished, out where the people who love the same things can find it. Ryan’s brief. It leads with our show your work philosophy and how we practise it, out of our own pages: Show Your Work, our Infodumplings post Show Your Work, One Card at a Time, Default to Open and our glossary’s Scenius. Austin Kleon’s idea and Brian Eno’s word are credited where they stand, every quotation was read on one of those pages, and each is checked against them word for word. Three places to show your work, for three lengths of time: the room’s channel on the CB for today, under Community on the chat page; Show your work in the forums for the longer write-up and the conversation after it; and the bench, for as long as you like. The bench holds only what its maker turned over, after our post’s line that turning a card over is the consent: every card says whose the work is as they asked to be named, where it lives, what state it is in, and whose words describe it, and comes down the moment its maker asks. To start it, the bench holds two unfinished things of our own, Cavendish Cards and this street, and ends in a blank card that asks what is missing. The Community Center’s service board has a slot for it. No photographs on the bench yet. Nothing on the bench is ranked or counted, nobody is pitched to or called a genius, and nobody’s draft is marked. The garage is lit by the day coming in through the open door, and nothing in it moves at any setting. Cabin Sketch, by Impallari Type, a typeface drawn with its pencil work left in, and Sen, by Kosal Sen, join the street’s faces, in the Foundry, the Mopery’s nook and the Open Notebook’s sticker drawer. A job for the Guild, a share card, a fractal window and liner notes come with the room.

item.title: The Source, up the hill behind The Feed, and both rooms’ channels hear what arrives
item.description: The Source opens behind The Feed (Ryan’s ask): white terraces under a warm spring, one pool for every repository on stimpunks.org’s feeds page, in that page’s order, and every commit a deposit in it, with its first line, its short id, its day and whose hands made it, off GitHub’s own commit feeds. Travertine is laid down a thin skin of stone at a time by the water that runs over it, which is how a repository is built too. Nothing on the hill is straight, and nothing is ranked or counted. The morning timers’ own commits are left off, and the morning task re-reads the terraces with The Feed’s boards. Whose hands is every name a commit gives: its author, and anybody its message credits in a Co-Authored-By line, which is very often Claude. Where GitHub names no author, the deposit says so, and an address is never read. The CB channels of The Feed and The Source hear each new item as it comes in, like a Discord feed bot (Ryan’s ask): every quarter of an hour our server reads every wire on The Feed’s boards and every spring on The Source’s terraces, and says anything new on that room’s channel under the room’s own name, marked BOT. Its first reading of a feed says nothing, nothing is said twice, and it never pushes a person’s message off a channel. Its name opens no profile and cannot be a username, nobody can edit what it says, and a moderator can take it off. Following the room by name tells you about each arrival; Follow every room does not. See the privacy page. The Feed loses its section about how the board is set and what it will not do, and the two lines under its lede saying when the whole board was set and counting its wires and rows: Ryan’s call, dry hedging that distracted from the page. That reverses what CLAUDE.md said the hall must carry. Every board still says the minute its own wire was read, which is what keeps the room from pretending to be live, and the refusals behind the section are still in tools/make-arrivals.py. Philosopher, Spline Sans and Spline Sans Mono join the faces; a job for the Guild, a share card, a fractal recipe, contrast pairs, liner notes, and a place on the map behind The Feed. Small screens and Print are now §124 and §125.

item.title: A Solarpunk patch at Brighter Days
item.description: A Solarpunk patch is lying in the shade under the first row of panels at Brighter Days Solar Farm, by the chiltepin, for your battle jacket (Ryan’s ask). It is shaped like one of the farm’s panels, tilted to the sun: deep blue glass with the faint lines of its cells, a hard white line of sun along its top edge, SOLARPUNK in the farm’s wide sun-yellow letters, a future with dirt behind our ears under it, and a sprig of small red chiltepin peppers growing out of a heap of soil at its foot. Like every patch, it is drawn only in its own room’s inks and lettered in its own room’s faces. The line is after Adam Flynn’s “Solarpunk: Notes toward a manifesto” (Project Hieroglyph, 2014), which says solarpunk is “a future with a human face and dirt behind its ears”. The patch says so beside it, and the liner notes credit him. Our glossary credits the line to a video; Star Stuff’s Shared Air zine traced it to Flynn, and the line was read in his piece before it went on the patch.

item.title: stimpunks.org’s form entries on the office’s dashboard
item.description: The office’s dashboard lists the latest form entries from stimpunks.org, first under Newest (Ryan’s ask): the highest WPForms entry number first, each with the form it came from (Request Aid, Request Creator Grant, Connect, Volunteer or Join Our Community), who sent it, the day, and the grant request or case it made, linked. Under them, how many came from each form this week and the week before. It is worked out from the office’s own records each time the dashboard opens and keeps nothing new. An entry from a form the office takes nothing from, or spam, never reaches the office, so the numbers skip, and the list says so. Each form type in data/office.json now names its form as stimpunks.org titles it, and tools/make-office.py refuses one that does not, or two that name the same form. Changed: netlify/cb/lib.mjs, office.js, data/office.json, tools/make-office.py.

item.title: A call for a moderator waits on the desk
item.description: When somebody who is not a moderator calls @moderator, on a channel or in a forum post, a note goes on the desk in the Moderators’ room as well as telling the moderators who asked to hear (Ryan’s call). So a call made while none of them was listening is still waiting: who called, when, where, linked, and the words they called with. An edit leaves one only if it newly calls. Nothing comes from a room that keeps to itself, or from one only some people may enter, and a moderator’s own call leaves no note. A moderator closes a note once the call is answered, which deletes it, and nothing says who closed it; one nobody closes goes after thirty days. A note stays if the caller takes the message off or deletes their username, as a report does. The privacy page says so. New: /cb/mod-calls. Changed: netlify/cb/lib.mjs, /cb/transmit, /cb/edit, /cb/forum, desk.js, town-hall-moderators.html, tools/check-push.py.

item.title: @moderator, @director, @board and @administrator
item.description: An @ can call a role now (Ryan’s ask), on a channel, in the forums, and in Tasks and the office. @moderator calls every moderator, and anybody signed on can call it, which is how to ask our moderators for help. @director, @board and @administrator can be called by our moderators, directors, board members and administrators. The roles you can call come first in the @ list, each saying what it calls. Everybody holding the role is told, and nobody is told who that is. On the CB and in the forums, the people holding it who switched on When somebody @mentions me are told where their pass can go, and the notification says which role; never in a room that keeps to itself. In Tasks and the office it goes into their Notifications there. A role called is drawn in a mention’s colour with nothing to press, filled in where you hold it, and a forum post calling a role you hold is under Mentions. The server decides which roles a message called, from the sender’s own pass and the words, never from what a page sends, and the word must stand alone: @moderators stays words. Those four words can no longer be claimed as usernames. The privacy page and the CB guide say so. Changed: netlify/cb/lib.mjs, /cb/transmit, /cb/channel, /cb/forum, /cb/tasks, /cb/office, cb.js, links.js, forum.js, tasks.js, office.js, comments.js, cb-sw.js, tools/check-push.py.

item.title: Your own cat at Pekoe and Purrs, and your own dog on the Run
item.description: A cat you adopted can be let out in Pekoe and Purrs, and a dog you adopted off the lead on the Run (Ryan’s ask). Signed on to the CB, Your own cat or Your own dog in the room lists yours, and one press lets them out among the animals still waiting for homes, where anybody who opens the room can meet them. Another press takes them home. They stay yours the whole time, three at a time at most. The room says they have a home and never whose. Their card says so where a waiting animal’s links to the shelter, and the list of who is in says it too. The animals waiting for homes come first: when every place is taken yours stay home, and if the shelter fills up while yours is out, the last one let out waits outside until there is a place. While a pet is out, the street keeps a copy of them in that room’s list, beside the scrambled form of your name and nothing about when. Taking them home, Forget me and deleting your username delete it; the privacy page says so. Both rooms’ pages no longer say every animal in them is waiting for a home. New: release.js, /cb/release. Changed: roam.js, purrs.js, run.js, the shelter’s answer, tools/make-pekoe.py, tools/make-the-run.py, tools/make-rescue.py, privacy.html.

item.title: Who’s online stays open
item.description: Leave Who’s online open and it is open again on the next page, and after a reload, until you close it (asked for by our community). Your browser keeps that in love-cb, beside the radio’s size and where you put it, and closing it forgets it. It still asks for the list only while the radio is open and listening: a folded radio sends nothing, whatever is open inside it. The privacy page lists it among what love-cb keeps. Changed: cb.js, cb-guide.html, privacy.html.

item.title: A community directory, and a tagline on every card
item.description: The community directory lists everybody on the CB who has chosen to be in it (Ryan’s ask), for anybody signed on: the avatar each person wears, their name, BASE for a moderator, their pronouns, their tagline and their nameplate, in alphabetical order. Pressing a name opens their profile, and Find somebody narrows the list by name, pronouns or tagline, in your browser, sending nothing. Nobody is in it until they tick Show my profile in the community directory, new at the foot of your profile card’s editor, which shows your line as it will look while the box is ticked. The directory says whether you are in it, with a button to your card, and Who’s around links to it. Clear my card, a moderator clearing a card, Forget me and deleting your username all take you out of it. A tagline on every card: one line of your own, up to 100 characters, under your name and pronouns, and beside your name in the directory. It never says how many people are in it, nor when anybody joined. The privacy page says what it keeps, and the CB guide how it works. Changed: directory.html, directory.js, directory.css, netlify/functions/cb-directory.mjs, netlify/cb/lib.mjs, cb.js, cb.css, profile.js, tools/make-profile.py, privacy.html, cb-guide.html.

item.title: Cloud City, a radio theme, a profile effect, a frame and a decoration
item.description: A Cloud City radio theme, Ryan’s ask, after the city in the clouds of Bespin in The Empire Strikes Back: dusk over a sea of cloud with the afterglow lying along it, a striped sun going down behind it, the city standing out of the cloud on its stalk with its windows lit, and cloud cars holding station, along the radio’s trims, dividers and sides. It is navy, cream, gold, peach and rose, the radio’s name and headings are in Jost, its corners are rounded over the top like the city’s deck, and every word clears 6.35 to 1 or better. It is a banner and a nameplate for profiles too, and Jost is offered for your name on your card. A profile effect, Cloud City, in the theme’s colours. Over your banner, the sky goes from night through rose to gold, a striped sun goes down behind the cloud, the city stands out of it with its windows lit, and two cloud cars hold station beside it. Cloud cars cross the profile now and then. When the profile opens, and once a minute, the sunset comes up over the whole profile with a sea of cloud along its foot, the city rises out of the cloud with its windows lighting from the top down, the sun sinks, and a pair of cloud cars flies out from the city towards you, fading after about nine seconds. A Portholes frame, the curved wall of a city in the clouds with a round window all the way round and a sunset in each, and a sunburst in every corner; and a Cloud cars decoration, a bank of cloud round the foot of your avatar with a striped sun going down behind it and two cloud cars going round the top. Both are in your card’s own colours. Nobody from the films is drawn, and no ship, emblem or lettering of theirs: the city, its cloud cars and the sunset are ours. Star Wars is a trade mark of Lucasfilm, and the credit on your card says so. Like every effect it moves only at MAX GLITTER or after Let my theme move, the cars drift forward and back and never round a loop, and nothing flashes. The liner notes and the CB guide say so. Changed: profile.js, cb-themes.js, call.js, cb.css, love.css, netlify/cb/lib.mjs, tools/make-profile.py, tools/check-contrast.py, cb-guide.html, liner-notes.html.

item.title: The notice can be put away
item.description: The notice along the top of the street has a Put it away button now (Ryan’s call), at the end of its line, or beside its horns on a phone. Pressing it puts it away on every page it is on, until a new notice goes up, and says so to a screen reader. The privacy page listed the key first: love-notice, in your own browser, holding a short code worked out from the notice’s words and nothing else. It is never sent anywhere, nothing tells us who put a notice away, and it clears itself once that notice is no longer up. Changing even a letter of a notice makes a new one, which comes back for everybody who put the old one away; the desk in the Moderators’ room says so, and its drawings are previews, whose button remembers nothing. Changed: notice.js, notice.css, netlify/cb/lib.mjs, privacy.html, the Moderators’ room and tools/check-notice.py.

item.title: A notice along the top of the street
item.description: Our moderators can put up one line along the top of the street’s front page, the Community Center, the forums and the office’s dashboard (Ryan’s ask), for everybody, signed on or not. The first is up already: our own Rando Calrissian launches Cloud Services. It is put up, changed and taken down at the desk in the Moderators’ room, which shows how it will look first and asks once more. One notice at a time, one line of up to 280 characters with bold, italic and links; a new one replaces the old, and the Brass Tacks Board is still where notices are kept. At MAX GLITTER it sparkles: stars twinkle along its rims, each on its own clock, and a fanfare plays once when it arrives or when the dial is turned up to MAX, two herald’s horns with notes rising out of their bells and a wave of sparks running along it. The fanfare makes no sound, because nothing on the street sounds until somebody presses something. Below MAX nothing on it moves, and at MAX nothing flashes and nothing crosses a word. It wears the CB’s clothes, because it is the CB’s: the radio’s colours, in the theme your radio wears on the page, or the forums’ and the office’s own. The privacy page says what it keeps: the words, and which moderator put it up or took it down last and when, shown only at the desk. Opening those pages asks for it once, with nothing of yours in the request. New: notice.js, notice.css, netlify/functions/cb-notice.mjs and tools/check-notice.py. Changed: netlify/cb/lib.mjs, desk.js, forum.js, office.js, forum.css, love.css, call.js, guest.js, the pages it is on, the Moderators’ room, privacy.html and cb-guide.html.

item.title: The channel comes first on the radio
item.description: The channel is straight under the room’s name now, rather than after Who’s around, Unreads and Events, which had pushed it too far down. Messages comes next. On the channel as and Be seen here have a part of their own, In this channel, as they do on the chat page, under Messages, with Bring my familiar, Join this room’s call and what is on now in the room. Where you are is the room’s name. Everything after that is in the order it was. At Full on a wide window the room’s name and the channel are the first column, wide, then Messages to Events, then the rest. The chat page is as it was. Changed: cb.js, cb.css and cb-guide.html.

item.title: Events on the CB, after Discord’s
item.description: Anybody signed on to the CB can schedule an event (Ryan’s ask and calls, after Discord’s scheduled events): on World or in a room they can go into, in its call, in the room itself, or at a link off the street, with a title, a date and time, how long it runs and what it is about. It can repeat every week, every other week, every month on the same weekday, or every weekday, and keeps to its maker’s clock when summer time starts or ends. Whoever scheduled it, or a moderator, can change it, cancel one time, or cancel it. Events is a part of the radio now, after Unreads, with what is on now in the room you are in, and on the chat page it is at the top of the channels and opens in the middle, at chat.html#events. Every time is in your own clock. An event names who is interested and never how many, the way a reaction does, where Discord prints a number on every event. I’m interested puts your username on its list, and Add to my calendar gives your device a calendar file of the next time, made in your browser and sent nowhere. Who sees one is who may go where it is: everybody on World, and in a room, whoever may go into the room, so an event in a Town Hall room or a staff category is only theirs. A room that keeps to itself has no events. Two more notifications, each off until switched on: When an event I’m interested in starts, up to five minutes before, and New events on World and in rooms I follow. Pressing one opens the chat page on that event. The privacy page says what is kept first: the event, its maker’s username and the usernames of everybody interested, and nothing about when anybody did anything. Forget me and deleting your username take your events and your name off every list. New: netlify/functions/cb-events.mjs, netlify/functions/cb-events-start.mjs, which tells starts every five minutes, and tools/check-events.py. Changed: netlify/cb/lib.mjs, cb.js, cb.css, cb-sw.js, privacy.html, cb-guide.html and tools/make-chat.py.

item.title: A topic’s controls go to its foot
item.description: In the forums, Pin, Close, Move, Tags, Add a poll and Take the topic down are at the foot of a topic now, under Change this topic, after the posts and the reply box. They used to sit between the title and the first post, and the list for moving a topic read as the category it was in, which confused people. Nothing stands between a topic’s title and its words now, reading it or editing it. Moving a topic names no category until one is chosen: the list starts on Choose a category, under the words Move it to another category, and Move with nothing chosen asks for one. On a new topic, Tags are under the words, with the pictures and the poll, rather than between the title and the words. Changed: forum.js, forum.css and cb-guide.html.

item.title: Join requests reach our Organizations page
item.description: A join request in the office can add an organization to our Organizations page on stimpunks.org, when they filled in that part of the Join form. A director names it (the form has not asked for the name), tidies its link and words, and chooses its ground. Check the Organizations page reads the page, says whose entry it goes after, and brings the logo they uploaded to look at; the director says in words what it shows. Add it to the Organizations page copies that logo into stimpunks.org’s media library and writes the entry at the end of the page. The logo goes with its camera data taken off: where it was taken, the device and the time, from a PNG, JPEG or WebP; anything else is added by hand. The privacy page said so first. Nothing else of their join request goes, and nothing is added if the page has changed since it was checked or something by that name is on it already. Both lines now take the name somebody asks to be shown by, once the Join form asks for it, and the Members page line falls back to the name they gave on the form. Changed: privacy.html, netlify/cb/lib.mjs and its tests, netlify/functions/cb-office.mjs, office.js, data/office.json, data/tasks.json, tools/make-office.py, architecture.html and cb-guide.html.

item.title: Join requests reach our Members page
item.description: A join request in the office can add somebody to our Members page on stimpunks.org, when they filled in that part of the Join form. It shows their line as it will look there, their name or pseudonym linked to their website and their words, in boxes a director can tidy first. Check the Members page reads the page and says whose line theirs goes after, and Add them to the Members page writes that one line at the end of its list. This is the first time the office writes to stimpunks.org, as one WordPress user with an application password: Ryan’s ask. The privacy page said so first. Nothing else of their join request goes, it never happens when a form arrives, and nothing is added if the page has changed since it was checked or somebody by that name is on it already. WordPress keeps the page as it was before as a revision. Changed: privacy.html, netlify/cb/lib.mjs and its tests, netlify/functions/cb-office.mjs, office.js, office.css, data/office.json, data/tasks.json, tools/make-office.py, architecture.html and cb-guide.html.

item.title: A CB invite in the welcome email
item.description: A mailing template in the office can hold {invite}, a link to join the CB. Writing to somebody with it, from their contact or now straight from their join request, the email waits for Make their invite: one press makes a CB invite that works once and runs out after thirty days, fills its link into the email, and then Gmail opens with it ready to read and send.
