Nobody has to visit the moderators’ desk and paste a code in. Its note says only that it was made in the office for one person, and nothing writes down whom it was for, on the invite, the contact or the join request, the same rule every invite keeps. Looking at a page makes no invite, each press makes a new one, and a mailing, which goes to many people, refuses a template with {invite} in it. Changed: privacy.html, netlify/cb/lib.mjs and its tests, netlify/functions/cb-office.mjs, office.js, data/tasks.json, tools/make-accounts.py, tools/make-office.py and cb-guide.html.

item.title: Join requests reach our mailing lists
item.description: A join request in the office now says which of our mailing lists they asked for on the Join form, the Members Only list and the Monthly Newsletter, and Add them to Givebutter’s lists adds them, on a director’s press. It sends Givebutter their name, their email address and the lists they said yes to, and nothing else of their join request. Givebutter finds somebody already there by their email and adds the lists without taking any away, and the join request then says which lists were sent and when. This is the first time the office writes to Givebutter, which until now it only read: Ryan’s call. The privacy page said so first. It is never sent when a form arrives, only on that press, so a spam entry never reaches a list. Changed: privacy.html, netlify/cb/lib.mjs and its tests, netlify/functions/cb-office.mjs, office.js, data/office.json, tools/make-office.py and cb-guide.html.

item.title: A window seat in the Community Center
item.description: The Community Center is a quiet room now, after somebody in our community asked for a softer look, in the biophilic, low-stimulation direction Ryan chose, with a sense of refuge. It is sage lime plaster with one big window facing north onto a hillside, so the light is soft and the same all day and no sun lands anywhere, and a deep seat is built into the bay under it, with a cushion, a throw and a plant on the sill. The stripes of sun behind every paragraph are gone, and so are the grid of the block wall over them, the black felt strips behind the headings and the orange stacking chairs. Every word sits on flat plaster now, the headings are the room’s rounded face in its own ink, and the front desk, the community service board’s pigeonholes and the member map are pale ash. It leans on 14 Patterns of Biophilic Design, by William Browning, Catherine Ryan and Joseph Clancy for Terrapin Bright Green (2014), credited in the room and in the liner notes: a view of a living hillside, a seat to look out from with the wall behind you, soft light, and lime, ash and wool. Nothing in the room moves at any setting. Its door on the street has a hill in its window, its share card is the window seat, and its job marker is a leaf fallen from the plant on the sill. The job is the same job, and anybody who had done it still has. Changed: community-center.html, love.css, index.html, design.html, liner-notes.html, README.md, fonts/_sources.json, data/quests.json, data/community.json, data/fractals.json, tools/make-og.py, tools/make-guild.py, tools/make-community.py and tools/check-contrast.py, and the notes in other rooms’ sections that described the old hall.

item.title: The member map zooms
item.description: The member map on the Community Center’s wall zooms now, after Ryan asked whether he could: with Zoom in, Zoom out and Whole world under it, and West, North, South and East to move it, so a keyboard can do all of it, and by hand with a double press, a pinch, Ctrl or Cmd and the scroll wheel, and a drag. The pins stay the same size while the world grows under them, so crowded places like the US east coast and Britain pull apart, and on a phone the numbers on the pins are as big as anywhere else. Pressing a pin says where it is. Zoomed in, the map shows Natural Earth’s lakes, the borders between countries and the lines between states and provinces, from our own site, asked for only the first time somebody zooms, so the map everybody sees first is no heavier. It jumps where you ask rather than gliding, at every setting of the dial. Changed: community-center.html, love.css, member-map.js, member-map-detail.json (new), data/world-detail.json (new), tools/pull-world-land.py, tools/make-member-map.py, tools/check-contrast.py and liner-notes.html.

item.title: The member map comes home
item.description: Our member map, of where our community lives, hangs on the Community Center’s wall now, a pull-down wall map in the hall’s own paint, in place of the Google My Maps map that stimpunks.org embedded. A pin says how many of us are in its place, Ryan’s call, and every place is listed in words below the map, by country. There is never a name. The 175 pins from the Google map came over with it, each only a place. We draw the world ourselves, from Natural Earth’s public-domain outlines, so looking at the map asks no map service or any other site for anything. stimpunks.org’s Individuals page can show the same map as a picture served from here. In the office, a join request has a Member map panel: the place they gave on the Join form is filled in, Find it looks it up on OpenStreetMap from our server, sending only those words, and Put it on the member map adds them, joining the place near it if there is one. Take them off the map is there too, and The member map, at the top of Cases, lists every place with how many are there. The privacy page says what the map keeps, and changed first; the Mission says the street counts people here too. Tested: places grouped with how many, no id or name in what anybody sees, a city kept as one place, a member moved and taken off, a deleted join request taking its pin, Google’s pins brought over once and one taken off by hand, and a lookup sending only a place’s words. tools/make-member-map.py holds it. Changed: community-center.html, love.css, member-map.js, office.js, office.css, netlify/cb/lib.mjs and its tests, netlify/cb/world.mjs, netlify/functions/cb-member-map.mjs and cb-office.mjs, data/world-land.json, tools/pull-world-land.py, tools/check-contrast.py, privacy.html, mission.html, cb-guide.html, liner-notes.html and the onboarding template.

item.title: The Join form reaches the office
item.description: stimpunks.org’s Join form now sends each new entry to the office, which finds or adds the contact, keeps the entry as a Join Request and makes the onboarding task in Tasks, as described below. The WPForms plugin there is at 1.2.0, which can map a form in a WordPress option as well as in wp-config.php, and the Join form is mapped that way. Entries sent before tonight stay where they were.

item.title: Onboarding a new community member: templates, the Join form and Gmail
item.description: Tasks has templates: a task to start from, with its name, description, tags, priority, who it goes to and when it starts and is due. Choose one under Start from a template when you make a new task, or press Make a task from it on its page. A name or description can hold {name}, somebody’s name, and {contact}, {case} and {grant}, links to their records in the office; you replace them in the form, and Tasks will not save a task from a template with one left in. Ryan asked for this to make onboarding a new community member less manual. Tasks starts with one, Onboard {name} into Community, whose checklist is the forum’s Onboard Community Member guide. When somebody fills in stimpunks.org’s Join form, the office now does the first steps itself: it finds or adds them as a contact, keeps their whole entry as a Join Request, a new type of case, and makes their onboarding task from that template, under nobody’s name, linking the join request and the contact, so each lists the task under Linked from. The task carries their name and none of their answers. If the template has been deleted from Tasks, the join request says no task was made. This needs the WPForms plugin’s version 1.1.0 on stimpunks.org and the Join form added to its settings there; until then Join entries stay on stimpunks.org as before. Write to them in Gmail, on a contact’s page, can take a template: choose one of the mailing templates and Gmail opens with their address, the subject and the words filled in for them, ready to read and send, such as the Stimpunks Community Membership Confirmation invite. A template that needs a grant request they have not made says so, and Copy the email is there for one too long to hand to Gmail whole. The office still sends nothing itself. The privacy page says what templates keep, that a Join entry makes a task, and what writing with a template does. Tested: the templates Tasks starts with, a template saved, changed and deleted, fill-ins refused where they do not belong, a Join entry making its case and its task once and linking both, a resend making neither again, a deleted template saying so, and every template filled in on a contact’s page. tools/make-tasks.py and tools/make-office.py hold it. Changed: netlify/cb/lib.mjs and its tests, netlify/functions/cb-tasks.mjs, tasks.js, office.js, office.css, cb-sw.js, data/tasks.json, data/office.json, both tools and privacy.html.

item.title: Wings on any chimera’s back
item.description: In Chimera Obscura any animal can have wings on its back now, spread behind its shoulders, and keep its own arms: a bear with an owl’s wings, a pig with a swan’s, a cat with a raven’s. A request in the suggestion box asked for wings. They come from the birds, each in its own colours, so the wings are the bird’s on any body: an owl’s, a raven’s, a swan’s, a chicken’s, a parrot’s and a roadrunner’s, chosen under Back like an armadillo’s plates. The turkey’s back is still its fan and the peacock’s its train. Changed: chimera.js, data/chimera-obscura.json and tools/make-chimera-obscura.py.

item.title: Chimera Obscura’s shelf takes to the water and the air
item.description: New on the shelf in Chimera Obscura, from Ryan’s list and a request in the suggestion box: a raven, a dolphin, a jellyfish, a narwhal, a swan, a chicken, a turkey, a parrot, a snake, a chameleon, a frog, an axolotl, a platypus, a beaver, a squirrel, a capybara, a Highland cow, a roadrunner, a peacock, a koi and an octopus. Every part of each goes with every part of every other animal, as before. They brought parts nothing had before, all drawn as code: a turkey’s fan and a peacock’s train for a back, a Highland cow’s shaggy coat with its fringe over the eyes, and a chameleon’s casque; horns, an axolotl’s gills, a chicken’s comb, and a roadrunner’s and a peacock’s crests where ears go; a raven’s bill, a parrot’s hooked beak, a swan’s bill and a platypus’s; a narwhal’s tusk, a forked tongue, a wattle, a beaver’s orange teeth and a frog’s grin; a snake’s slit eyes, a chameleon’s turrets and a frog’s eyes up on the top of its head; tentacles, fins and a jellyfish’s streamers; a jellyfish’s bell and a capybara’s square head; a koi’s barbels; a snake’s coils, spots, a koi’s patches and a macaw’s bare face; and a neck, so a swan, a turkey, a roadrunner and a peacock hold their heads up. Some animals give a part by not having one: a snake’s arms and feet, a jellyfish’s arms and a frog’s tail are none, so a bear with a frog’s tail has no tail, and the words beside the table say whose it is. Feathers on a dark wing are drawn light, so a raven’s wings, a macaw’s blue ones, and an owl’s in a panda’s colours show their feathers, where before they were drawn dark on dark. The test that draws every pair of animals with every part from either now lets parts that never shape each other travel together (arms with feet, the mouth with the ears, the colours with the markings), so it still draws every pair and runs in about the time it did before the shelf grew. It was broken on purpose and still caught it. Changed: data/chimera-obscura.json, chimera.js, chimera-obscura.js, tools/make-chimera-obscura.py and tools/chimera.test.mjs.

item.title: The moderators’ desk: everybody, and kick, time out and ban
item.description: The desk in the Moderators’ room lists every username on the CB, says how many there are and how many are seen in a room now, and shows who is seen and where. A name opens its profile; At the desk looks it up. Moderators asked for it for safeguarding, and it is Ryan’s call, which reverses the street’s rule that there was no list of everybody, for moderators or anybody, and his call that the rule against counting people is about the street’s public surfaces and not about moderation; the Mission says so now. Seen means they pressed Be seen here, by the same rules as Who’s online: a room that keeps to itself is never named. So the list never calls anybody offline: everybody not seen may be on the CB too. It shows nothing else about anybody: not when they joined, not an email address, not anybody’s roles beyond moderator, and nothing records who looked. A username looked up at the desk can be kicked, timed out or banned. Each signs it off every device at once. A kick is only that; a time out keeps it off the CB for ten minutes, an hour, a day or a week, reading included; a ban keeps it off until a moderator lifts it, and holds the name so nobody else can claim it. Signing on, the person is told a moderator timed them out and for how much longer, or banned them, and where to reach us, and only after the right password, so nobody else who tries the name learns anything. Only until when is kept: not which moderator, not why. The desk does none of the three to a moderator’s username. The radio and the rooms no longer say the password has changed when a username is signed off, because a moderator may have signed it off: they say it was signed off since you signed on. The privacy page says all of this, and changed first, as did SECURITY.md, whose note on accounts was out of date. Tested: a kick, a time out that ends and is not kept, a ban that holds until lifted, a wrong password learning nothing, recovery refused while barred, and the list showing only what it should. tools/make-accounts.py holds each promise, and was broken on purpose. Changed: netlify/cb/lib.mjs and its tests, netlify/functions/cb-account-admin.mjs, desk.js, town-hall-moderators.html, love.css, cb.js and the rooms’ scripts that said the password had changed, privacy.html, mission.html and SECURITY.md.

item.title: Every sign-on note says invite
item.description: The notes shown to somebody not signed on, beside the things only a CB username can do, still said those things took a CB handle and the community password, which retired on 2026-10-21. Each now says it takes a username on the CB, which you join with an invite, and links to Getting started at the Community Center, where the front desk is too: on Count Me In’s stair, Pando Calrissian’s tree and fence, Plural Mural’s chalkboard, the Fridge of Sighs, the three shelters, and the pebble bowls in the Faery Yurt and the Solarpunk Hermitage, which tools/make-pebbles.py writes.

item.title: The Community Center’s door says invite
item.description: The Community Center’s door on the front page still said to sign on with a handle and the community password, which retired on 2026-10-21. It says now that you join the CB with an invite and a username and password of your own, which is what Getting started says inside.

item.title: Community Care: the street’s room for asking
item.description: Community Care is a shopfront on the street, between Chimera Obscura and Your Room: our mutual aid and care room. Its channel on the CB is where you ask for mutual aid, peer support and any other help, and where anybody who can offers it, and it is under Community on the chat page, beside World, the Community Center and Dead Tired Society, whose page now points to it for peer support. Ryan’s brief. It is built out of three pages of ours: Community Care, our glossary’s Peer Support, and Tuesday Ferguson’s Tapping the Radical Roots of Peer Support. Every quotation was read on one of them, is credited to whoever said it, and is checked against them word for word. The channel is for four things, after a line of Vivian Ly’s at Autscape 2020: asking, offering, receiving and declining, and all four are allowed. Vivian Ly’s talk, which our Community Care page carries, is in the room to press, and says how long it runs first. Nobody who asks is sorted, owes anybody or proves anything, and nothing is counted. The room says it is not a crisis line and where the crisis lines are, says who can read the channel and how long a message stays, points to the forums’ Mutual aid and Coping for asks that need longer, and names the Foundation’s grants without promising them: they are by application, in scheduled rounds, and cannot cover anything urgent. The room is a street roofed with everybody’s umbrellas, tied to one another, in the rain, after our Community Care page’s umbrella and its photograph of umbrellas strung over a street. Nothing else holds the roof up. At MAX GLITTER the rain falls on it, and never under it. The Mission’s limit said this street is not mutual aid, which a room for asking for it would have made untrue. It says now that the street is not the foundation’s mutual aid: it still pays no rent, buys no groceries and gives no grant, and Community Care is where people ask each other. Agbalumo, by Raphael Alẹ́gbẹ́lẹ́yẹ̀ with Sorkin Type and Eben Sorkin, and Ysabeau Infant, by Christian Thalmann, join the street’s faces, in the Foundry, the Mopery’s nook and the Open Notebook’s sticker drawer. A job for the Guild, a share card, a fractal window and liner notes come with the room.

item.title: A poll can be added to a topic that has started
item.description: A topic without a poll has Add a poll at its top, for whoever started it, the editors of a wiki it is in (Grantmaking’s directors and board) and our moderators. The poll stands under the post that opens the topic, as one made with it does, and whoever added it can close it too. A poll is never added over one that is there, because its votes would go, and never to a closed topic. Adding one posts nothing, so reply if you want people to know.

item.title: Polls in the forums: a show of hands, or a sealed ballot
item.description: A topic can open with a poll, Norah’s ask: Add a poll under a new topic, with a question, two to twenty choices, one or several to pick, and a day it closes if you like. Its starter or a moderator closes it. A show of hands shows everybody who can read the topic who picked what, as the votes come in, and a vote can be changed or taken back while the poll is open. A sealed ballot keeps nothing that says who picked what: how many picked each choice, and apart from that who has voted, as a code that differs in every poll. So nobody can see anybody’s vote, moderators included, a vote cannot be changed or taken back and asks a second time before it goes, nobody sees a number until the poll closes, and once its results are out it stays closed. This reverses the forums’ rule that nothing in them is counted, for polls alone, Ryan’s call: a poll says how many picked each choice, in its own order, never sorted by it and with no winner marked. The Mission says the street counts people in two places now, the World room’s Most active order and these, and the privacy page says what each kind keeps.

item.title: The newest email and the team mailbox’s counts on the office’s dashboard
item.description: The office’s dashboard lists the newest email filed, under Newest: each one’s subject, which contacts it came from or went to, and when, linking to the email. Until now the office kept no list of recent email, only each contact’s own; it keeps the twenty newest now, sealed, for the dashboard alone, with no address and no word of an email in it. The team mailbox counts itself once an hour for the dashboard: unread conversations in the inbox, the emails that came in and went out in the last seven days against the seven before, and how many of those were with one of our contacts. Numbers only, so nothing about anybody leaves Gmail for them. The dashboard says when they were counted, and says a count could not be finished rather than showing a smaller number. The counts start once the team mailbox’s script is updated. The privacy page says what both keep.

item.title: Messages on the chat page, and links named for their own site
item.description: Your conversations are in the chat page’s list, under Direct messages after Community, and the one you pick takes the channel’s place in the middle, as tall as the page, rather than squeezing into the right-hand column. All messages is the list itself, with Let people message me. Your conversations are kept out of the page’s address. The CB guide has more. A link whose words name its own site is a link now, so [Chat — Stimpunks.World](https://stimpunks.world/chat) on the channel is a link to the chat page rather than the Markdown as typed. Words naming any other site still keep a link as typed, so nothing can pose as somewhere it does not go. Messages’ Open button stays inside a narrow radio, at Full and on the chat page.

item.title: The chat page: every room’s channel on one page
item.description: The chat page is every room’s channel on the CB in one place, laid out the way chat is: the channels down the left, the one you pick in the middle with what its room is about, and who is around on the right. It is the radio itself, docked into the page in your radio’s theme, so replies, reactions, pictures, Be seen here and each room’s call all work there. The channels are in three groups: Community, which is World, the Community Center, Dead Tired Society and every room at Cavendish Coworking; Staff, which is the Town Hall’s private rooms and the forums’ staff categories, shown only to the people who can go in; and World, which is every other room. A channel with something new in it is in bold with a dot, never a number, and a box finds a channel by its name or what its room is about. The channel you pick is in the page’s address, so Back goes to the one before and a link can open on one, like chat.html#the-den. It changes nothing about the radio on any other page. The CB guide has the rest.

item.title: Grant rounds in Grantmaking, and tags in the forums
item.description: Notion’s Grants table now lives in the forums’ Grantmaking, rather than in a copy of Notion’s databases: every grant round is a topic tagged grant-round, and the rounds from the table were brought in at the time each was made, under the username that made it, with its grant type and approvals at the top. Each says it was brought from Notion. Topics can carry tags, up to five words, and a category’s page can show only one tag’s topics. Tags are never counted. The CB guide has how. Grantmaking keeps its topics for good, not for six months, and any director or board member can edit the post that opens a round, so each can add their name to its approvals, as in Notion. Replies stay their writers’ own. A Grant Round template is in Team Docs’ Templates, with the sections the table’s own template had and the grant-round tag, which comes with it.

item.title: Buttons for formatting, and links without Markdown
item.description: Every Markdown box in the forums, Tasks and the office has buttons over it, for the many of us who would rather not write Markdown: Bold, Italic, Link, List, Numbered, Checklist where it fits, Quote, Heading and Code, with Ctrl or Cmd and B, I or K. To make a link, highlight the words and press Link, then give the address; or paste an address over the highlighted words. The CB guide has the rest.

item.title: The office’s Newest, by the day they were submitted
item.description: The grant requests and cases under Newest on the office’s dashboard are the ones submitted last. They were the ones added last, and a batch brought over from EspoCRM had put requests from 2023 at the top.

item.title: The forums’ @ list offers more people
item.description: Typing @ in the forums offers anybody who started or last posted in a topic you can read, as well as the topic’s own people and anybody on Who’s online, so a new topic, or one only you have posted in, offers names too. If you can open Tasks, it offers everybody Tasks can assign. They are names you can already see on Latest; there is still no list of every username.

item.title: Tasks and the office, for the board too
item.description: Everybody on the board can open the office and Tasks, as our directors and administrators could, and can be given a task. They share one rule, so the one change opens both. Privacy and the CB guide say so.

item.title: Moderator, shown as a role on the desk
item.description: The roles on the desk in the Moderators’ room start with Moderator, ticked for everybody on the list, and the button puts somebody on the list as a moderator, so a moderator who is not a director, on the board or an administrator is one press: their username, nothing else ticked.

item.title: Back Office Operations, for our moderators too
item.description: Every moderator can read and post in the forums’ Back Office Operations, and hear its room on the CB, as well as the directors and the board. Being a moderator already opened the CB’s moderation tools, the Moderators’ room and the Moderators and Team Docs categories.

item.title: Roles, kept at the desk
item.description: Our administrators give and take moderators’ roles at the desk in the Moderators’ room: who is a moderator, and who also holds board, director or administrator. Until today the list was only in the site’s settings. A few names stay on a break-glass list in the site’s settings, which the desk shows and cannot change, so nobody can be locked out. Board is given or taken only by somebody on the board or that list, because Executive Session is the board without staff, and nobody can be left without an administrator. A role given or taken needs no signing off: the person’s radio picks up their new pass by itself. Privacy says what the list keeps: who changed a name last and when, and nothing more.

item.title: Mentions in Tasks and the office
item.description: An @mention in Tasks is drawn as the person’s name and opens their profile, in descriptions and comments, and in the office’s comments, as it already was on the CB and in the forums. Yours is marked. Type @ and a name in a task’s description or any comment there or in the office, and pick from the list of the directors and administrators.

item.title: Links and Linked from, after Notion’s
item.description: Type [[and part of a name in a message on the CB, a forum post, a task or a comment, or a record in the office, and pick a forum topic, or for our directors and administrators a task, a grant request, a case or a contact, to link it. It is drawn as what it is and its name. A link never carries a name. The name is shown only to the people who could open it; everybody else sees that it is one they can’t open. Linked from, on a task, under a topic and on an office record, lists what links to it, of what you could open yourself. Chats can hold links and are never in it, because the CB keeps them for 48 hours. Privacy says what it keeps.

item.title: Previews in the lists, and the forums one press away
item.description: Rest the pointer on a task’s name in Tasks’ list, or on a grant request’s or a case’s in the office, and a preview shows beside it, Norah’s ask: what happened to it last, the first parts of its description and its latest comments. Landing on the name with the keyboard shows it too, Esc puts it away, and the pointer can move onto it to read it. The forums’ bar has Tasks and Office for our directors and administrators, and Tasks’ bar and the office’s have Forums, so each is a press from the others.

item.title: Tasks: Group by
item.description: Tasks’ list can be grouped, after Notion’s By assignee: Group by Whose puts each task under every person on it, assigned or also on it, so each person’s heading has all of theirs. Tags, Assigned to, Status and Priority group it too, a heading folds its group away, and a saved filter keeps the grouping. A filter saved in the feed is kept now. Until today the server refused it.

item.title: Tasks: coloured statuses, and Whose
item.description: A task’s status is a coloured pill now, after Notion’s, in the list, on the board, in the feed and on the task: Not Started gray, Started the light blue Notion gives In progress, Completed green, Canceled brown and Deferred yellow, each with its name on it. Tasks’ list has a Whose column: who it is assigned to and who else is on it, together, so you can sort by everybody on a task.

item.title: The office and Tasks, one press apart
item.description: The office’s bar has Tasks, and Tasks’ bar has Office, at the end of each, so you can go back and forth. The office’s dashboard starts with Newest and Open tasks by person, then the figures, and each list in Newest is headed by a link to its own page: the grant requests, the cases, everybody’s tasks and the forums’ latest.

item.title: Invites, and every username claimed
item.description: You join the CB with an invite now. A moderator makes one at the desk in the Moderators’ room and shares its link, which opens the joining page: choose a username and a password of your own, keep the recovery code, and you are on. An invite can be for one person or many, and runs out after a day, a week, a month or never. Nothing records who joined with which invite; an invite counts its uses and that is all. The starter password is retired, Ryan’s call, and it signs nobody on. This reverses what the street did since the CB opened: claiming your username was optional until today. If you are on with the starter password, the radio asks you to claim your username before anything else, and everything kept under it stays with it. A moderator’s username is claimed on the joining page with the moderators’ password, which signs nobody on either. CLAIMED is gone from the channel, the forums and profiles, because every username is claimed. BASE still marks a moderator. An email address for password recovery, if you want one. This reverses “no email”, Ryan’s call. Give one when you join, or under Account on the radio, and Email me a reset code at the front desk sends a code from our team’s mailbox, good for an hour. It is kept sealed and shown to nobody but you. What it keeps, and who handles it.

item.title: The office opens on its dashboard
item.description: The office opens on its Dashboard now, and the contacts have moved to Contacts in the bar. The dashboard’s Newest has the forum topics posted to last, of the ones you may read, beside the newest grant requests, cases and tasks, each saying its category, who posted last and when.

item.title: Tasks: comments brought over from Notion
item.description: The comments on our tasks’ pages in Notion are on those tasks in Tasks now, each under its writer’s username at the time it was written, among the task’s other comments, and saying in Notion. Their writers can edit them here. Bringing them over told nobody. Bringing comments over again changes the ones already brought rather than adding them twice, leaves alone one edited here, and leaves deleted one deleted here. A few that named members of the public were left in Notion.

item.title: The office: comments on templates and emails
item.description: A mailing’s templates and the emails filed from the team mailbox take comments too, at the foot of their pages in the office, sealed like every other comment there. They tell people as the office’s other comments do, saying only that they are on a template or an email. Every template has a page of its own, opened from the list: its subject and words, who added and changed it, Edit, Send it as a mailing and Delete, and its comments. Saving one goes back to it.

item.title: Tasks and the office: comments
item.description: Every task in Tasks has Comments, after EspoCRM’s stream posts and Notion’s comments: the conversation about it, under its description, oldest first, with a box at the foot. A comment takes Markdown and has Preview; Ctrl or Cmd and Enter posts it. So does nearly everything in the office: every contact, grant request, case and mailing, at the foot of its page, encrypted where they are kept like everything else there. A comment tells the people it concerns, in their Notifications in Tasks and on their devices if they switched that on: for a task, whoever it is assigned to, anybody else on it and whoever made it; in the office, whoever added the record; and anybody who commented before and anybody it @mentions. It says who commented and on what, never the words, and opens on the comment. A comment in the office never names its record there. Only whoever wrote a comment can edit it, and an edit tells only somebody it newly @mentions. Its writer or an administrator can delete it. Both Feeds show each card’s latest comments and have Comment on every card, and a comment puts its card first. Privacy and the CB guide say what is kept.

item.title: Tasks and the office: a Feed, after Notion’s
item.description: Tasks has a Feed beside the list, the board and the timeline: every task as a card, the one something last happened to first, saying what that was, with its description to read and tick, More for the rest of it, and Mark it completed. The filters and saved filters work on it as on the others. The office has one too: grant requests and cases, and contacts if you ask for them, newest first, each with its description or notes, and Move to on a grant request or a case. Neither keeps anything: both are worked out from what Tasks and the office already hold, twenty cards at a time.

item.title: The CB: Read aloud
item.description: A message’s three dots have Read aloud, on the channel and in direct messages: that one message, read out now in the same voice as Speak new messages aloud, whether that switch is on or off. It says who sent it, whose message it replies to, its words, and what its picture or sticker is. It stops whatever the radio was saying first; while it reads, it says Stop reading, and pressing it stops. It keeps Speak aloud’s rules: a voice built into your own device and never a speech service somewhere else, and the static round it follows the dial. The CB guide says so.

item.title: The CB: replies
item.description: Every message on the CB has a Reply, a curved arrow between React and the three dots. It opens Replying to their name and the start of their words above the message box, and what you transmit goes out as an answer, with that line above it on everybody’s radio. Press the line to go to the message it answers. Cancel reply or Escape lets it go and keeps your words. Direct messages have it too, once a conversation is accepted. A reply keeps which message it answers and nothing else of it. The line is drawn from what is on the channel now, so it changes when that message is edited, and says the message has gone once it is taken off or its 48 hours are up. Copying the quoted words into the reply would have kept them after the message, and after somebody took them back. When somebody replies to me is a new notification switch, off until you switch it on, and Everything takes it in. It tells only whoever sent the message answered, and never in a room that keeps to itself. The CB guide and the privacy page say so.

item.title: Notifications: follow every room
item.description: Notifications on the radio have a Follow every room too, under Rooms you follow: every message in every room you can go into tells your device, and with Calls on, every call starting in one, including rooms that open later and the forums’ categories you can read. Norah’s ask, after the one for Unreads this morning. It can be a lot, and the switch says so. World keeps its own switch, and Everything leaves this one as you set it. Switched off, you are back to the rooms you followed one by one. A room that keeps to itself still tells only a device that followed it there by name, so its own switch stays in it. The CB guide and the privacy page say so.

item.title: The CB: follow every room at once
item.description: Follow every room, at the foot of Unreads on the radio, follows every room you can go into at once, instead of pressing Follow this room in each. Unreads then lists any room where something new has been said since you last read it, in the street’s walking order, including rooms that open later and the forums’ categories you can read. Norah’s ask. Switched off, Unreads goes back to the rooms you followed one by one, which it keeps as they were. It is kept in your browser only, like the rooms you follow, and a room that keeps to itself is never on it. The CB guide has it. It is for Unreads; notifications still follow the rooms you pick under Notifications.

item.title: Tasks, the office and the forums: back one step, to where you were
item.description: Going back in Tasks, the office and the forums goes back one step now, to the view you came from, at the height you left it, with the keyboard on the link you followed, once the view has drawn. Norah’s ask, and Ryan’s for the scroll. Your browser’s Back and Forward do it, and so does a link above every view you reached from another one, which says where it goes: ← Back to the board, say, or back to a task by its name. A view opened on its own keeps its old way up, like ← All contacts. Contacts you had shown with Show more, and older topics you had opened in the forums, are shown again when you go back to them, so the place is still there. Drawing the same view again, as Forget what I have read does, keeps your place too, where it used to jump to the top. Saving, cancelling, sending or deleting takes the place of the step it was done on rather than adding one after it, so Back never lands on a form you finished or something that has been deleted. The tab’s own history keeps how far down each view was, beside its address, so a reload or coming back from another page finds your place as well; never a name or a word of what is in them, which the privacy page says for each of the three. The CB guide has it.

item.title: The forums: every category has its own channel on the CB
item.description: Every category in the forums is a room on the CB now, instead of the whole of the forums sharing one channel. Open a category, or a topic in it, and the radio’s This room retunes to that category’s own room, The forums: Coping, say, with its own channel, Be seen here, call and Follow this room. Move to another category and it follows, without the page loading again. The forums’ home, Latest, Mentions and Search are still The forums’ own room. Ryan’s ask and his calls. A category’s room is for exactly the people who can read the category: a claimed username, with the category’s own roles, checked by our server for listening, sending, hosting a film, being seen, the call and notifications. So the channels of Moderators, Team Docs, Directors, Board, Back Office Operations, Grantmaking and Finance are their staff’s alone, as their topics are. A category inside another shares its room, so all of Team Docs is one. Category rooms are kept off the street’s public list of rooms. The radio asks which ones you can read, so #tags, the teleporter, Who’s around and Unreads only ever name a category to people who can read it. In the World room, The forums’ line takes in what is happening in the categories you can read. The privacy page and the CB guide say how it works.

item.title: Tasks: brought over from Notion
item.description: The tasks made in our Notion since they were last brought into EspoCRM are in Tasks now, with their status, days, tags, priority and who is on them. Each says it came from Notion and links its page there. Notion does not say who made a task or when it was finished, so those are left blank rather than guessed. Bringing tasks from Notion again updates the ones already brought rather than adding them twice, and one deleted here stays deleted, as with EspoCRM’s. Copies Notion’s recurring templates made of a task Tasks already makes were left out.

item.title: Tasks: notifications on your phone or computer
item.description: Something new in my Notifications in Tasks is a new switch under Notifications on the radio, for our directors and administrators, off until you switch it on. With it on, a device is told whenever something arrives in your Notifications in Tasks, with who did it and the task’s name, and pressing it opens the task. Your own changes never are. The privacy page says what a notification carries.

item.title: Four more paintings in the yurt, three more spines, Feldman and Fisher in the Cinema
item.description: Four more paintings hang on the yurt’s gallery wall, at Helen’s ask: Burne-Jones’s The Beguiling of Merlin, Waterhouse’s The Magic Circle and Hylas and the Nymphs, and Edward Robert Hughes’s Night with her Train of Stars, each out of copyright everywhere and each scan carrying a public domain template on its own Commons page. The Golden Stairs was the first choice and was left for Merlin, because neither scan of it carries that template. Agnes Martin, Hiroshi Sugimoto and James Turrell are spines on the Art shelf in the Reading Room, each a door to their page on Wikipedia, because their work is still their own. The Cinema’s Art shelf has Morton Feldman’s Rothko Chapel, the music he wrote for the chapel, played by Les Cris de Paris and the Ensemble intercontemporain on their own channel, beside the chapel’s own film; and its Philosophy shelf has more Mark Fisher: his Demonstration of Capitalist Realism from Artists Space, Kodwo Eshun’s memorial lecture from Goldsmiths, Acid Horizon on his final lectures, and two films from Epoch Philosophy.

item.title: #3ecologies in the Music Room, sparkling skies behind the portals, and one reel off the Cosmos shelf
item.description: The Music Room links to #3ecologies on YouTube Music, at Helen’s ask, under the record case. It is a search there, so it is a link that opens on YouTube Music and nothing plays here. At MAX GLITTER the stars behind the yurt’s portal doors sparkle once the doors are open, at her ask: every star twinkling at its own pace and four-pointed glints flaring and fading across each sky. At Gentle and Regular the skies stay still, and nothing flashes. Helen’s ballroom photograph hangs above the Music Room’s doors in the yurt now, at her ask, with its caption about the library turning into a masquerade ballroom. The Cinema’s Cosmos shelf lost one reel, at her ask: a fan’s upload of the first episode of Carl Sagan’s Cosmos, which was not its rights holder’s.

item.title: The yurt’s doors open onto space, and the Cinema has a book
item.description: The doors to the Music Room, the Reading Room and the Cinema are portals now, at Helen’s ask: the Glimmer Window’s oak doors in their stone arch, the same size, and behind each one deep space, a sky of its own for each room (a violet nebula and a ringed planet, a moonlit constellation, a spiral galaxy). Open them and step through. The words under every door go through too, without opening anything. The books in the yurt are smaller when shut, so the portals are the big things on the page; each opens out to its full size to be read. The Cinema has a book in the yurt, bound like the songbooks: every reel on its rails, shelf by shelf, each line a link to that reel. Nothing in it plays. Two more shelves in the Cinema: Films I Love, official trailers for films that are hers to love and yours to buy, rent or find elsewhere, and Things That Make Me Smile: Curb Your Enthusiasm from HBO, Peep Show, Frasier from Paramount+, Gilmore Girls and Jeff Arcuri, every one from its own official channel. Fan uploads were swapped for the official ones, and one trailer with no official upload anywhere was left off.

item.title: The Cinema, behind the yurt, with a reel for every film
item.description: A cinema door in the Faery Yurt opens the Cinema, at Helen’s ask: an old picture-house arch in the yurt’s timber with its screen lit and a film strip winding across the front of it, under a new heading of its own, The Cinema. Every film she keeps is an old-fashioned reel on a rail on the wall, in rows rather than a bookcase, on shelves under her own headings: Philosophy (lots of Deleuze and Guattari, Bergson and Merleau-Ponty (Absurd Being’s podcasts on both, and lectures), Mark Fisher’s The Slow Cancellation of the Future, every talk of Robert Chapman’s that could be found, Astrida Neimanis on bodies of water, and Philosophy Tube), Nature, Cosmos, Weird stuff (ContraPoints), Art (Rothko and Goldsworthy, from Tate, MoMA, the Rothko Chapel and the National Galleries of Scotland), Ma, Minimalism & the Void, Poetry (Sylvia Plath and T. S. Eliot reading their own) and Relaxation. A reel can be one film, a whole channel or playlist that plays from the top with the rest to scroll through in the player, or a live camera: the Monterey Bay Aquarium’s jellies and the Okaukuejo waterhole in Etosha. A film says how long it runs before the press, a channel or playlist that it runs until you stop it, a live camera that it runs until you close it, and nothing plays until then. Every reel was pressed on the screen and played before it went up: where one of National Geographic’s playlists would not play in the United Kingdom, the reel holds its whole channel instead. The Reading Room’s card catalogue has The Deleuze Seminars, his lectures online at Purdue University, on the Gilles Deleuze card, at her ask the same morning. It is the Reading Room’s house two doors along, like the Music Room: claret walls, velvet curtains tied back from a silver screen, a candle in a sconce on each wall, three rows of velvet seats, and the light coming over your head from the projection box with the house lights down. The projector never flickers; its two reels turn at MAX and nowhere else. Join the Faeries and Grow a garden are in there too. A job marker of its own, a ticket stub dropped under a seat, on the guild’s board; a card, a place on the map and a fractal window, like every room.

item.title: Tasks: activity and notifications
item.description: Every task in Tasks shows its Activity: each change made to it, newest first, who made it and what it changed from and to. A description’s change says only that it changed. Notifications, beside the other views, list the changes to the tasks you are assigned to, are on or made, being put on or taken off one, a task a recurring task made for you, and @mentions of you in a description, with how many are unread in the bar and your tasks due today, tomorrow or overdue at the top. Your own changes are never there, and nobody else sees your list. The privacy page says what is kept.

item.title: The office: Givebutter on the dashboard
item.description: The dashboard in the office reads our Givebutter account late each evening, and when asked, and never writes to it. It shows what was given in the last 30 days against the 30 before, the recurring plans and what they give a month, every month of the last year, each campaign and what it has raised, and the newest gifts. Nobody who gave is named: the office keeps no donor’s name, email, phone or address, as the privacy page says. The QuickBooks summary now names only the kinds of transaction there were, so a month of deposits is no longer called deposits, payments and sales receipts.

item.title: The office: each night, the CB’s days, and QuickBooks
item.description: The dashboard in the office keeps a line each night of how many grant requests, cases and tasks were open, and draws them as lines from the first night on. It shows how many messages went out on the CB each day for the last month: a count and nothing else, with no name, no room and no words, as the privacy page says. The office can be connected to our QuickBooks. It reads the books late each evening, and when asked, and never writes to them; the dashboard shows the last 30 days of money in and this year’s income and expenses by month. Each pipeline is held to its own cap of 100 on the dashboard and in Reports. The first version put both pipelines’ requests against one cap.

item.title: The office: a dashboard and EspoCRM’s reports
item.description: The office opens a dashboard of what came in this week against the week before, open grant requests against the cap of 100, open cases and tasks, and the newest of each, with charts of EspoCRM’s four dashboard reports. Its summary is plain sentences built from the same numbers. Reports has all nine of EspoCRM’s reports, from grant requests by year and grants awarded by year to the grantees of any year and cases by status and year. Every chart says its numbers and has them in a table under it. Cases no longer have the Invited In and Collaborating statuses, which were being retired; no case was at either.

item.title: The office: a mailing can start from a day
item.description: A mailing in the office can be narrowed to the grant requests submitted since a day, because a stage like Granted holds everybody who ever reached it. This year fills in the first of January. The preview says how many earlier requests it left out, the second press says so again, and sending is refused if the day changed after the preview.

item.title: The office: mailings to a grant stage
item.description: A director can email everybody at one stage of a grant pipeline from a template, from the office: Email everyone at a stage on the grant requests list, or New mailing. Templates take fill-ins such as {first}, {grant} and {amount}, and refuse one the office does not know. Every email is shown filled in first, with everybody left out and why, and sending asks again, naming everybody it goes to. The team mailbox sends them within ten minutes, one email to each person, and each is filed on its contact. Anybody who asked not to be emailed is left out. A mailing can be stopped while emails wait. Privacy says what a mailing keeps, and that it is the one time the office hands the mailbox’s script anybody’s address.

item.title: The office: a Gmail label adds somebody new
item.description: Somebody who writes to the team mailbox and is not in the office yet can be added from Gmail: put the Office label on one of their emails, on the web, on a phone or with a filter, and within ten minutes they are a contact, with the whole thread on their page. For an email we started, whoever we sent it to is added. Only the name and address on the email go, and only for the emails somebody chose to label; everybody else’s email still stays in Gmail. Privacy says so.

item.title: The office: email with the team mailbox
item.description: Email between the team mailbox and somebody in the office is filed on their page, as EspoCRM did: newest first, each saying whether it went to them or came from them, and whole when opened, with its attachments named. A script inside the team’s Gmail sends it, every ten minutes, signed with a key of its own. Only email with a contact leaves Gmail. The script is given a keyed hash of each contact’s address rather than the address, and sends an email only when somebody on it matches. Attachments stay in Gmail. Writing stays in Gmail. Write to them in Gmail, Open the thread in Gmail and Reply in Gmail open it there, signed in as the team mailbox. Privacy says what the office keeps of an email.

item.title: The office takes stimpunks.org’s forms, and EspoCRM goes
item.description: A request for a grant, a connection or a volunteer application on stimpunks.org now arrives in the office, sent by stimpunks.org’s server and signed with a key the two servers share. The person is found by their email or added, and their grant request or case is made, once, however often it is sent. EspoCRM is no longer used for anything. Its tasks, contacts, grant requests and cases are all here, and the forms that fed it feed the office instead. Privacy says how an entry arrives.

item.title: The office: cases
item.description: Connection requests and volunteer applications are in the office, which EspoCRM called cases, each keeping its number, sealed at rest like everything there. A list and a board by status, as grant requests have, opening on the open cases. A contact’s page lists their cases beside their grant requests, and starts a new one from them.

item.title: The office: grant requests
item.description: Our grant requests are in the office, beside the contacts they come from, moved from EspoCRM: Mutual Aid and Creator Grants, each at a stage of its pipeline, sealed at rest like everything there. A list and a board, after EspoCRM’s: filter by pipeline, stage and status, each choice saying how many it would show, with what the shown requests come to; or see one pipeline’s stages as columns and move a card by dragging it or by its own Move to. A contact’s page lists their requests, and starts a new one from them.

item.title: The office: contacts
item.description: The office opens, for our directors and administrators: the people and organisations we are in touch with, moving here from EspoCRM after tasks, with grant requests and cases to follow. A list a hundred at a time, a search over names, emails and phone numbers, sorting, and each contact’s page with their notes in Markdown. Everything in it is encrypted where it is kept, under a key only the site’s functions hold; without the key the office is shut. Nothing about a contact is ever logged, nothing records who looks, and a search is never put in the page’s address, where the browser’s history would keep it. Privacy says what it keeps.

item.title: Tasks: tag colours
item.description: Tags have colours, a dot beside every tag’s name in Tasks, by what the tag is about: running things blue, money orange, people aqua, gatherings yellow, words magenta, the shop green, and looking after ourselves violet. The timeline’s bars wear them: each bar filled with its first tag’s colour, and striped along its foot when its tags have more than one, with a legend above saying which is which. The colours change step for light and dark radio themes so the words on every bar can be read.

item.title: Tasks: yours includes the ones you are also on
item.description: A task is yours when it is assigned to you or you are also on it, and Tasks open on yours now, in the list, on the board and on the timeline. Whose picks everybody’s, one person’s, or the ones assigned to nobody. Who else is on a task shows everywhere: a column in the list, a line on each board card, and on the timeline a task stands in the row of everybody on it, marked ALSO ON IT where they are not the one it is assigned to.

item.title: Tasks: a timeline
item.description: Tasks have a timeline, beside the list and the board: a row for each of us, the days running across, and each task a bar from the day it starts to the day it is due. Show a week, 2 weeks or 4, and move along with Earlier, This week and Later. The list’s filters work on it, and a timeline can be a saved filter. That finishes moving the team’s tasks off EspoCRM: the tasks, the list, the board, saved filters, recurring tasks, checklists and the timeline are all on the street now. The CB guide has how.

item.title: Tasks: checklists you tick in place
item.description: A checklist in a task’s description is boxes now, as it was in EspoCRM: write a list item as - [] or - [x], and on the task you tick it where it stands. A tick changes that box and nothing else, so two people ticking at once both keep theirs. The CB guide says how.

item.title: Tasks: the recurring ones are made here now
item.description: The team’s recurring tasks are made on the street from today, not in EspoCRM: EspoCRM’s twelve are switched off and ours on, each with the same next day. The first one made here is the Weekly Editorial Meeting on Thursday. Tasks › Recurring has them all.

item.title: Tasks: recurring tasks
item.description: Tasks can come round again, as they did in EspoCRM: weekly, every 2 weeks or monthly. On its day a recurring task makes its task by itself, starting and due as many days after that day as it says, and its name can carry the week, the year or the month. Each recurring task shows its next three tasks and the tasks it has made, and a task it made says so. Switch one off and it makes nothing until it is switched on again. The team’s twelve from EspoCRM are here, switched off until EspoCRM’s own are. The CB guide has how, and the privacy page what is kept. A timeline comes next.

item.title: Tasks: a board, and saved filters
item.description: Tasks have a board, beside the list: the same tasks in columns by status, priority or who they are assigned to, each column saying how many it holds. Drag a card to another column to change it, or use the card’s own Move to, which works from a keyboard, a screen reader and a phone. The list’s filters work on the board too. Saved filters. Save a list or a board as it is, filters, order and columns, under a name, and it is there on any device you sign on with, saying how many tasks it shows now. They are yours alone. The CB guide has how, and the privacy page what is kept. Recurring tasks come next, then a timeline.

item.title: Tasks: the team’s to-do list, on the street
item.description: Tasks are the team’s to-do list, moving here from EspoCRM. Only our directors and administrators can read them, signed on to the CB with a claimed username, and they wear your radio’s colours, like the forums. The list shows every task with its status, priority, who it is assigned to, the days it starts and is due, and its tags, and says how many tasks match. Filter by words in the name, who it is assigned to, when it is due, status, priority and tags, each choice saying how many it would show, and sort by any column. The filters and the order live in the page’s address, so a bookmark or a link keeps them. A task has a Markdown description, people working on it beside whoever it is assigned to, and says who made it and who changed it last. Edit it, mark it completed, or delete it. Kanban and saved filters, recurring tasks, and a timeline come next, in that order. The CB guide and the privacy page say all of this.

item.title: A page in the Wiki or Team Docs can be as long as a long document
item.description: The page that opens a topic in the Wiki or Team Docs can be 150,000 characters now, so the team’s longest documents go up whole as they move out of Google Docs, board minutes with their transcript included. Every other post, a reply on a page included, is still up to 20,000. The CB guide says so.

item.title: Team Docs in the forums, with templates and pictures in the words
item.description: The team’s documents can move out of Google Docs and into the forums. A new staff category, Team Docs, is for our moderators, directors, board and administrators only, keeps everything for good, and every page in it is a living document any of them can edit, as in the Wiki. Inside it are Field Guide, Notes, Meeting Minutes and Templates. A category can hold other categories now. They stand under it at the side and on its page, and its page lists every topic in it and under them. Meeting Minutes holds a category for every year from 2024, and a new one arrives by itself each January. A new topic can start from a template. Pick one over the title and press Use it, and its title and words go in for you to fill. The templates are the topics in Team Docs’ Templates, so the team keeps them up to date in the forums, the way it kept them in a folder before. A pinned one there is its read-me, not a template. A picture can stand in the middle of a post’s words, for a screenshot at the step it shows. Paste a screenshot straight into the box you are writing in, drop a picture on it, or press Put it in the words, and it goes in where the cursor is. Everywhere else, pictures still sit below the words. A page in the Wiki or Team Docs holds thirty pictures and files, for a how-to with a screenshot for each step; any other post, six. Tables were already there, and now the forums say so: a row to a line, a | between cells, and a line of dashes under the first row. Their headings are bold now. The CB guide and the privacy page say all of this.

item.title: The street on your Home Screen and in your Dock
item.description: People are adding stimpunks.world to their Docks and Home Screens, so we checked it behaves there. Chrome says it can be installed from every page, and it keeps a back button in a Mac’s Dock and in Chrome’s window, because a street of pages with no way back is a maze. Installed, each room still colours the window’s bar its own way. On an iPhone or iPad, notifications need iOS or iPadOS 26 or later. Older versions save the street to the Home Screen as a Safari bookmark, and a bookmark cannot notify; from 26, every site added to the Home Screen opens as a web app, and notifications work. The CB guide, the privacy page and the radio’s Notifications tray said any iPhone would do, and say iOS 26 or later now. Added to a Home Screen or a Mac’s Dock, the street starts afresh, because Apple keeps an installed web app’s storage apart from Safari’s: you sign on to the CB again there, and the dial and the animals you rescued start again too. The CB guide says so. Installed from Chrome or Edge, you stay signed on. On Android, a CB notification’s little picture in the status bar is the heart now, where it was a plain white square. And the manifest, which tells an installed app its name and icons, says which app it is, so an install made before today stays the same app, and a change to it reaches installed apps without waiting out a week’s cache.

item.title: Albums and playlists play on the first press
item.description: Every album and playlist button on the street now plays when you press it. In these rooms a whole list only got ready when pressed, and you had to press play a second time inside the player: the records and the cave’s speaker at the Solarpunk Hermitage, the YouTube deck on Club Chronic’s stage, both decks at Pink Pony Club, the chancel in The Chappell, and the screen at Black Leather Lagoon. A single video already played on its press, and so did the lists in the other rooms. Now these do too. Nothing reaches YouTube before you press, the same as before; the press that asked for the list now plays it.

item.title: Follow keeps going through an album
item.description: Following somebody through an album now goes on from song to song. Helen hosted the John Coltrane and Johnny Hartman album at the Solarpunk Hermitage, Ryan pressed Follow, and his playback stopped at the end of every song. Each song in an album is a video of its own, and the radio was treating each new one as a film to get ready on its own: when a moderator is hosting, that puts the song by itself on the Hermitage’s television, where it plays to its end and stops. Now a host’s radio says which album or playlist the song is in, and Follow keeps pace with the whole list: when the host goes on to the next song, yours does too, and if they skip to another song, yours goes there, to the same place in it. Pressing Follow before you have started anything gets the album’s own play button ready at the host’s song and place, and nothing goes up on the television. Catch up moves an album you are already playing to the host’s song and place, and still never presses play: it plays if yours was playing and waits if it was not. Two smaller faults went with it. For about half a second between songs, the player still gives the last song’s title with its clock back at 0:00, and a host’s radio that spoke then told everybody the album had gone back to the start of that song; now nothing is said until the next song has started. And Follow used to take any stop for your own pause: now only a pause does, so a song that ended before the host’s waits for them, and a next song your player would not start is started, and the radio says so if it still will not. The privacy page says what a host’s radio now sends: the album’s or playlist’s YouTube id, beside the song’s own.

item.title: Your strip in the Dress-Up Den and Fantasy Fancy Dress, and a curtain at the back
item.description: Your strip is in the Dopamine Dress-Up Den and Fantasy Fancy Dress now, as well as the Bodymind Booth, so you can walk into either room on your own and bring back an avatar you kept. Signed on to the CB, press Open my strip: in the Dress-Up Den a bodymind comes back in with everything it had on, and an outfit goes back on the stand, ready to change and keep; in Fantasy Fancy Dress a bodymind comes into the fitting with its wings and ears and everything else, and when you take it back through, the Dress-Up Den knows which one it is, so Keep the changes changes that one. Opening your strip only asks your Profile for what you already kept, and only when you press it. Nothing in Fantasy Fancy Dress is kept, and the privacy page says what opening your strip sends. The way through to Fantasy Fancy Dress is a curtain you can see. It was a link in a sentence near the top of the Dress-Up Den, easy to miss; now it is a doorway at the back of the shop, its curtain in moons and stars drawn back with gold rope, the back room dark beyond it with a light at the far end, and a button under it, Through to Fantasy Fancy Dress. Press the curtain or the button. Your bodymind still goes through with you, and so does which avatar it is.

item.title: Howling Wolf, Starward Dreaming, Leaping Dolphins and Autumn Falls
item.description: Howling Wolf is a new profile effect: a wolf sitting on a crag against a full moon, raising its head and howling, with stars, cloud and a far ridge of pines over your banner. When your profile opens, the night comes up over it, the moon rises, the wolf howls and two wolves on the far ridge answer. Nothing makes a sound. Starward Dreaming looks up through a clearing in the trees at the stars and the Milky Way, from beside a fire you cannot see: its light is on the trunks, its flames lick up over the foot, and its embers rise and become stars. When your profile opens, the trees close round the whole of it, a shower of embers goes up and becomes stars, and a star falls. The flames sway slowly and never flicker, so nothing in it flashes. Leaping Dolphins is dolphins leaping in arcs across a sea dappled by the setting sun. When your profile opens, the sunset comes up over the whole of it and a pod of dolphins leaps across, one after another. Autumn Falls is a big tree in red, orange and gold, its leaves drifting down into piles, and children popping up out of them, with one in a wheelchair beside them throwing leaves up. When your profile opens, leaves come down all over it, pile up along its foot, and the children pop up out of the piles. Each is drawn in colours of its own over whatever card it is on, because moonlight, firelight, a sunset and an autumn afternoon with children in it are colours a card’s own cannot hold. As with every effect, the part that crosses your words, and the opening, are drawn only at MAX GLITTER or after Let my theme move.

item.title: Sit in the cozy, in any room with one
item.description: Press your familiar in a room with a free cozy and Sit in the cozy is there, beside Move it, wherever the cozy is on the page. It used to show only once a cozy was already in view, so it was easy never to find. If the cozy is out of view, your familiar goes to it and the page brings it into view.

item.title: An egg chair at the Hermitage’s campfire
item.description: The Solarpunk Hermitage has a Chimera Cozy: an egg chair on a swivel foot, standing on the green shag in front of the campfire’s television, its pale shell lined in the cabin’s mustard and outlined like everything else on that rug. A familiar that finds it free sits in it to watch. A familiar sitting in a cozy draws its light in to just behind it, so you can see what it is sitting in. Sit in the cozy no longer scrolls the page back to where your familiar was just before it moves.

item.title: Familiars stop walking back in from the corner every few seconds
item.description: A familiar kept vanishing and walking back in from off the page to where it was sitting, every few seconds, in a cozy or not. The check it makes now and then of where the page has put it moved it to the corner to measure, and if its last move had been a walk, the browser walked it back. It reads where it is now and never moves to measure, and a check in the build refuses the old way.

item.title: Familiars find their cozies, and keep out from under the radio
item.description: A familiar goes to a free cozy when one comes into view, at MAX GLITTER or when you let it move by itself: after you scroll, and when the page or the radio changes. Before, it only looked for one when it arrived or now and then while wandering, so it could sit beside a free cozy and never use it. It no longer sits under the radio. The radio’s box counts as somewhere it cannot rest, so a cozy the radio is covering is not free, and a familiar the radio opens over moves out from under it. Make the radio smaller and the cozy is free again. Sit in the cozy, when you press your familiar, puts it in a free cozy in view at any setting, as dragging it next to one already did. A familiar waits for the room to settle before it sits down, so a cozy that comes into view once the page’s typefaces are in is not missed.

item.title: Bring my familiar shows for moderators, and says where a familiar comes from
item.description: Bring my familiar was hidden from moderators signed on with a password of their own, because the radio did not count a moderator’s own password as a claimed username. It does now. With no familiar following you, while you are seen in a room, the radio now says so under Be seen here, and where to take one from: Chimera Obscura, or your chimeras in Profile. Once one is following you, the switch is there.

item.title: Familiars in company, with sayings and cozies, and a possum and an opossum
item.description: Other people’s familiars, in the room with you. With a claimed username, switch on Bring my familiar under Be seen here on the radio, and the people seen in the same room as you see your familiar there, as you see theirs. Press one to see whose it is and hear one of its sayings. It is off until you switch it on, it is never on Who’s online, and the privacy page says what is kept. Chimeras have sayings. Write up to five beside its name, on the bench in Chimera Obscura or in Profile under Its name and sayings. A familiar says one when you press it, and now and then in a speech bubble when it may move by itself; they show under your chimeras in your profile too. Chimera Cozies. Some rooms now have a spot of their own for a familiar to sit in, each drawn in that room’s own colours: a velvet pouf in Chimera Obscura, a cushion of moss in the Garden, a knitted floor cushion in the Latibulum and a leather footstool in the Community Library. A familiar sits in a free one, and at MAX GLITTER they wander between them. Through the door. At MAX GLITTER, or when you let it move by itself, your familiar walks into each room from where it was when you left the last one, and other people’s walk in from the edge of the window when they arrive and out to it when they go. A possum and an opossum are on Chimera Obscura’s shelf: the brushtail, with big dark eyes and a dark bushy tail, and the Virginia opossum, with a white face, black ears and a bare pink tail.

item.title: Familiars: a chimera that follows you from room to room
item.description: A chimera can come with you now. Take it with you in Chimera Obscura, or Take it with me on one of your chimeras in Profile on the radio, and it becomes your familiar: it is there in every room you walk into, in a little pool of the camera obscura’s light. The idea came from our community, after the animal orbs in Castle Crashers. It sits wherever there are no words. It finds a clear spot in each room, off the text, the buttons, the pictures and the players, and if the page changes under it, it moves aside. It only crosses words while it is on the move. It stays where you put it unless the dial is at MAX GLITTER, or you press it and switch on Let it move by itself. Then it wanders now and then, comes along when you scroll, and comes over to wherever your pointer or your keyboard has gone. At Gentle it jumps rather than walks. Press it to move it (drag it, or Move it and the arrow keys), put it back on the table in Chimera Obscura, or Send it home. It keeps you company and that is all it does: no levels, no boosts, nothing to collect, and nothing counted. It makes no sound. Your browser keeps it, and nothing is sent anywhere: what it is made of, its name, whether it may move, and roughly where in the window you last put it down, never which room. The privacy page lists it as love-familiar. Nobody else sees your familiar. It stays out of Stay Frosty, where nothing moves, and the Healing Checkpoint.

item.title: Messages stay together at Full
item.description: At Full, on a wide window, a channel with only a few messages no longer spreads them down the whole column with their words far below their names. The log is as tall as the column, and its messages now sit together at the top of it, as they do at every other size.

item.title: The CB marks what is new to you, and Unreads lists it
item.description: A dot now marks what has been said since you last read it, on World, This room, Your messages and each conversation in it. That reverses the radio’s old rule of no badge and no unread count, and only as far as a mark: it is never a number, it makes no sound, and nothing moves. A screen reader hears “something new”. Unreads, a new part under Who’s around, lists World, the rooms you follow and your conversations while something new is waiting in them, and takes you there. Follow this room, beside This room, puts a room on it; which rooms you follow stays in your browser. It needs a claimed username. So that reading on your phone clears the dot on your laptop, the street keeps when you last read each channel and conversation, and nothing else, for 48 hours at most; the privacy page says so, and Forget me deletes it.

item.title: Paste a picture, and messages that work like the channel
item.description: Paste a picture into the CB with Ctrl or Cmd and V, on the channel or in a conversation, instead of finding it with Picture. It comes to the same preview, redrawn the same way before it goes. Words pasted with it are pasted as words. Direct messages work like the channel. Each message has React and the three dots on its line: Copy, Edit and Take back on yours, Copy and Report on theirs. Sticker sits beside Picture and opens the same tray. Reactions say who, never how many. An @name is drawn as a name. A first message is still words only, so a picture, a sticker and a reaction wait until the conversation is accepted.

item.title: Profile opens folded up
item.description: Every section of Profile starts folded, so opening it shows a short list of headings: your profile card, props, avatars, chimeras, pets, badges and jobs, and battle jacket. Press a heading to open that section, and again to fold it; open as many as you like. Each is fetched from the street only when you open it, so opening Profile is quicker and asks for less. A props notification still opens Profile straight at Your props, opened.

item.title: Account: your username and Forget me, out of Profile
item.description: Your username and Forget me have a button of their own, Account, beside Profile under the radio’s heading You. Claiming your username, changing its password, its recovery code, deleting it, and Forget me are all there now, and Profile is what you show: your card, your sets, your props, avatars, chimeras, pets, badges and battle jacket. Account ends in Close Account, like the other long trays. Everything that told you to claim your username in Profile says Account now: the Community Center’s steps for claiming, the CB guide, the privacy page, the shelters, the Bodymind Booth, the moderators’ desk, the forums and the Adventurer’s Guild’s shelter jobs.

item.title: A Close at the foot of every long tray on the radio
item.description: Profile, Themes, Notifications, the stickers and Your messages each end in a button that closes them: Close Profile and the rest. You no longer have to scroll back up past everything in a tray to find the button that opened it, and closing puts you back on that button, where the tray began.

item.title: Profile and Sign off under a heading of their own, and open trays that look open
item.description: Profile and Sign off are under a new heading on the radio, You, just above Your radio, and Profile’s tray opens under it. With Profile open it was easy to lose where the tray began, and to scroll past the top of it looking for the button to close it; the heading marks where it starts. Profile, Notifications and Themes are edged in the readout’s amber while their trays are open, as Who’s online already was, so you can see which one is out.

item.title: Bigger headings on the radio, and Be seen here says whether it is on
item.description: The headings between the radio’s parts are bigger, Where you are, Who’s around, Channel and the rest, so they are easier to find. In a theme whose lettering runs small they grow as far as they can while the room’s name stays the largest words on the radio. Be seen here says whether it is on: Be seen here: off and Be seen here: on, the way the switches under Your radio and in Notifications do, so you can tell at a glance.

item.title: @mentions, links with words, headings, a look at your picture, and the radio in a window of its own
item.description: Type @ in the CB’s message box and it offers people to mention, the way # offers rooms: everybody who has spoken on the channel, everybody they mentioned, and everybody on Who’s online, alphabetically. Arrows move, Enter or Tab puts the handle in, Escape leaves what you typed. A mention is drawn as the person’s name, which opens their profile, and your own name is filled in where you are mentioned. Nothing lights up or chimes when one arrives, and a device that asked to be told about mentions is told, as before. A place in a film, @34:12, is still a place in a film. A link on the CB can have words of its own: [words](an address). That reverses a rule the radio has kept since links arrived, that a link’s words were always its address, and the reason for the rule still holds: a link to another site still says which site after its words, so no words can make it look like a link on the street, and words that are an address themselves, like [paypal.com](…), are not made a link at all. The CB guide and the house norms say so. # A heading, with a space after the #, is a heading in a message, and ## and ### smaller ones. Without the space, #the-den is still a room. A picture is shown before it goes. Pick one and the radio shows it above the message box, the moment it is chosen and then as it was redrawn, which is exactly what will be sent, with the name of the file you picked, so you can see it is the one you meant. In a conversation under Messages too. Pop out, under Your radio, moves the radio into a window of its own, as big as it is and at the size it is, like a call’s Pop out, and it stays open while you go from room to room in the window you came from. It follows you: This room, Be seen here, the room’s call and the teleporter are the room that window is on, and a link on the channel opens there. An @time and Catch up move the film in that window. Every other page has a small bar where the radio was, with Show it and Bring it back, so there is only ever one radio listening. Host this film and Follow stay with the radio in the page.
