Speak new messages aloud works again. Since yesterday it had been saying nothing: the list of messages on the channel and the radio’s note that it was speaking had the same name, and the list being there stopped the voice from ever starting.

item.title: Profile sets: save a look and wear it again with one press
item.description: Your profile card’s look can be saved under a name and worn again with one press, asked for by somebody in our community who keeps a few favourites to switch between by mood, by the room they are in and for what is on: Otters, Halloween, Fairy Lights. Your profile sets, in Profile under the card, keeps each one: its theme, banner, decoration, frame, effect, name face and nameplate, and the avatar you wear. Pressing a set puts it on your card at once, and the one on your card says so. Change under each set updates it to your card as it is, renames it or deletes it. Your words are not in a set. Your pronouns, what you wrote about yourself, your links and your favourite room stay as they are whichever set you wear, so something you rewrote last week is never put back by a press. Nobody else sees your sets: your profile shows only what is on your card, not what sets you have or which one you are wearing, and nothing records when you made or wore one. Privacy and the CB guide say so. Claiming your username no longer signs the radio off by accident. If the radio was in the middle of listening at the moment you claimed, that listen came back refused for the handle’s old pass and the radio said the password had changed. Only a refusal of the pass it holds now signs it off. And once you press I have kept it, your profile card and your sets are there in Profile at once, rather than after you open it again. Changed: cb.js, cb.css, netlify/cb/lib.mjs, netlify/cb/lib.test.mjs, netlify/functions/cb-profile.mjs, netlify/functions/cb-pets.mjs, tools/make-profile.py, privacy.html, cb-guide.html.

item.title: Pictures in messages, every notification at once, and new lines on a phone
item.description: A direct message can carry a picture once the conversation is accepted. Somebody in our community testing the Sandbox had a screenshot to show Ryan and no private way to send it. Picture now sits beside Send in a conversation both of you have started, and a first message is still words only, so nobody’s first contact with you can be a picture. It is the channel’s picture: redrawn in your browser first, which takes off what the camera wrote into it, with a description if you like, fetched by the two of you and nobody else, and gone when its message goes. A reported picture goes to the moderators’ desk with its message, where it waits behind Show the picture. Privacy and the CB guide say so. Everything, and anything added later is a new switch at the top of the CB’s Notifications, asked for by the same person after new switches arrived off overnight. It switches on every kind of notification there is, every message on World included, and any kind added after you press it, so you do not have to come back and look. Switch any one off and the rest stay on. It leaves the words, and the rooms you follow, as you set them. On a phone, Return makes a new line in the CB’s message boxes, and Transmit, Send or Save sends, because a phone’s keyboard has no Shift and Enter. The box starts four lines tall there, and its words are big enough that an iPhone no longer zooms in when you tap it. On a computer, Enter still sends and Shift and Enter still makes a new line, and Ctrl or Cmd and Enter sends anywhere. Changed: cb.js, cb.css, cb-sw.js, desk.js, love.css, netlify/cb/lib.mjs, netlify/functions/cb-dm.mjs, netlify/functions/cb-dm-reports.mjs, the new netlify/functions/cb-dm-image.mjs, tools/check-messages.py, tools/check-push.py, privacy.html, cb-guide.html, town-hall-moderators.html.

item.title: Flying Fairy, a profile effect, and a Fairy Lights theme
item.description: A profile effect, Flying Fairy, Ryan’s ask. The faeries of Helen Edgar’s Faery Yurt fly across your profile, from either side, darting and hovering with their wings going, no two dressed alike, each dropping petals behind it, and petals drift down across the profile now and then. A garland of fairy lights hangs over your banner with a faery sitting on it and another hovering, and there are roses, a daisy and sparkles in the corners. When the profile opens, and once a minute, a dusk comes up over the whole profile with sparkles along its top, and a big fairy rises into it: red hair under a crown of roses and two little curled horns, a cloak of moss, a posy of red and pink roses held close, her eyes shut. She opens her butterfly wings and beats them slowly while petals and leaves fall round her and three of the yurt’s faeries fly out from her, and after about nine seconds she fades. She is our own drawing, after the look of Helen’s own profile. A Fairy Lights radio theme, grown from the Fairy lights frame for profiles: its strings of bulbs, swagged across a plum night in gold, rose, mint, sky, lilac and peach, with stars between them, along the radio’s trims, dividers and sides. The radio’s name is in a soft script, and every word clears 4.5 to 1. It is a banner and a nameplate for profiles too, drawn at whatever height it has, and the face is offered for your name on your card. Like every effect, it moves only at MAX GLITTER or after Let my theme move, and the bulbs twinkle slowly; nothing flashes. The liner notes and the CB guide say so. Changed: profile.js, cb-themes.js, call.js, cb.css, love.css, netlify/cb/lib.mjs, tools/make-profile.py, tools/check-contrast.py, cb-guide.html, liner-notes.html.

item.title: Who is hosting moves to Watching together
item.description: Who is hosting a film is under the CB’s Watching together now, headed Hosting now, asked for by Ryan. It was in the readout under the messages, where a line saying somebody was hosting read as the newest message. Catch up and Follow moved with it, beside a host in your room. The radio answers Catch up, Follow, Host this film and Screen a video under them, in Watching together, so the sentence saying what you are hosting and who can see it is there too. While the radio is Small, which shows only the channel, the answer is under the readout as before.

item.title: The CB points at the World room
item.description: Under the CB’s Channel, beside the line about the forums, a line now says where to find the rooms active now and the calls going: the World room, asked for by Ryan. It is left off in the World room itself. Calls going now, under Who’s online, lost the sentence under its heading, which said again what the heading says. Who is in a call is still shown only in its room, to anybody seen there, and the CB guide and the privacy page still say so.

item.title: A screen in every gallery of the Jungle Room
item.description: The Jungle Room has a screen at the top of every gallery, asked for by Ryan: any cam can go up on its gallery’s screen with the button under its leaf, so watching one big never means scrolling back to the top of the room. Every cam still opens in its own leaf where it hangs, the same size as before. A screen shows nothing of its own and loads nothing until you put a cam on it. Until then it is a low gap in the leaves; when a cam goes up it opens to the size of the picture, and the line under it says what is on and that it runs until you close it. Taking it off leaves the screen empty again. Each gallery’s leaves fold away, so a gallery you are not watching is one line. The cams whose owners have switched off embedding are still doors out to YouTube, with no screen button, because a screen could not show them either.

item.title: Everybody down at the Watering Hole
item.description: The Watering Hole’s drawing has everybody who comes down to the water, asked for by Ryan: elephants, springbok, gemsbok, zebras, rhinos, giraffes, gnus and ostriches, the animals people have seen on the waterhole cams. An elephant drinks with her trunk while her calf waits, a giraffe splays her legs to reach the water and another browses the camel-thorn, the gnus come in single file, and a rhino brings her calf down. It is still noon, so every shadow is straight under its animal, and the springbok leaping in the foreground has left hers on the ground. More of the pan, too: mud cracking round the edge, tracks going down to the water, dry grass, rings where somebody is drinking, a far tree on the plain, and a round rock in the middle of the pool, which is the real Namib waterhole’s. Nothing in the drawing moves. The Okaukuejo waterhole in Etosha is on the rack, after the Namib: the floodlit one, where elephant and rhino come in after dark. It is the Jungle Room’s cam, read out of that room’s own list, so it plays here or on the screen by the water and says what it is before you press it.

item.title: The CB as an icon, and as the whole window
item.description: The radio has a size smaller than Small, asked for by Ryan: an icon of a CB set, the aerial, the readout and the handset on its coiled cord, drawn on the radio’s own case in whichever colours you have chosen. − from Small makes it one, and pressing the icon opens the radio at Small again. Drag it to put it somewhere else. The icon is still on. It listens, so a film you are hosting or following carries on and Be seen here still holds, and Fold away is still the only off. Nothing on it changes when a message comes in, and a screen reader hears nothing new at that size; the CB guide says Small is the size for keeping an ear on the channel. And a size larger than Large, for anybody who wants to see only the CB: Full fills the window, with the channel as tall as it is. On a wide window the parts stand in three columns, where you are and who is around on the left, the channel in the middle, and messages, watching together and your radio on the right, each scrolling by itself. It stays put, and a room’s call window stays on top of it. Pressing the middle of Move’s six dots works now. It landed on the drawing of the dots rather than the button and did nothing, drag or press, so only the edges of the button moved the radio.

item.title: A screen in the rock at Big Steep
item.description: Big Steep Fermentables has a rack of somebody else’s cellars under a screen in the rock, asked for by Ryan, with seven more videos he picked: a rainy evening in an old wine cellar, a wine bar by a fire, a velvet wine cellar, an underground wine cellar, wine cellar ambient music, a fantasy tavern and a cellar soundscape. Each says how long it runs before you press it, plays where it hangs or goes up on the screen, and was checked on its own watch page first. The screen has nothing of its own on it, because the cellar has no whole list to put on, and it is not lit: it is a dark pane in the racks’ steel, and the room’s light still comes only through the drinks. It is the room’s first screen, so it is where the CB puts things: somebody can host what is on theirs and others can follow, and a moderator’s Screen a video goes up on it, waiting for each follower’s own press. The wine bar only plays on YouTube. Its channel has switched off showing it on other sites, so its card is a door out, dashed and with no screen button, and says why on its face. Two of the new videos play on into YouTube’s own mix, as the speakeasy already did, because that is how Ryan sent them. Their labels give the first video’s runtime and say nobody here has checked what the mix plays after it. A mix now starts on the first press in its card, where before it loaded a second play button.

item.title: A Treasurer in the Town Hall
item.description: Mila Krambo is on the walls of the Board room and Executive Session, as our Treasurer, elected Treasurer and director at the board meeting of 29 September 2026. Both rooms list the board as our Board & Governance page does, in its order and with its titles, and her name goes to her section of our About page.

item.title: A wiki in the forums
item.description: The forums have a Wiki, under Information: how to do things on the street, the CB and the forums, one thing to a page, for the questions people keep asking. The first pages cover making and dressing an avatar, editing your profile, writing in Markdown, changing your password, joining a call, choosing a CB theme, adopting a pet, making a chimera, collecting patches and badges, finding who’s online and which rooms are busy, giving props, and reporting bugs and asking for features. Every page is a living document. The post that opens each topic in the Wiki is a WIKI PAGE, and our moderators can edit it whoever started it, so the pages can be kept up to date as the street changes. Each says who started it and who edited it last. Replies stay their writers’ own, and only they can edit them, as everywhere else in the forums. Pages in the Wiki are kept for good. Something wrong or missing on one? Reply on the page, or ask in the Help desk. Privacy and the CB guide say what changed. Fixed: a forum post, a suggestion or a Brass Tacks plate with https:// in it and nothing after it, as in “an address starting with https:// becomes a link”, could not be sent: the forums said they were busy. It turned up while the Wiki’s page on Markdown was being written. Those words stay words now.

item.title: Direct messages on the CB
item.description: The CB has direct messages, in a new part of the radio called Messages, under the channel: one person writing to another, which people have been asking for as our community moves off Discord. Both of you need a claimed username, because an unclaimed handle is anybody’s who signs on with it. Nobody new can write to you until you switch on Let people message me, and somebody’s first message waits for you to answer it, press Accept, or press Reject, which deletes it and tells nobody. They can write nothing more until you do. To write to somebody, press Message under the card in their profile, or type their username under Messages. Every message goes 48 hours after it was sent, like the channel. You can edit your own messages or take them back. Block stops somebody writing to you and deletes your conversation, and they are not told. Report sends a copy of one message they sent you to the moderators’ desk, which is the only way a moderator ever sees a message. They are not end-to-end encrypted, and the privacy page says exactly what that means. Nothing counts them and nothing says whether somebody has read one or is typing. Switch on When somebody messages me under Notifications to be told when one arrives.

item.title: Be told when somebody gives you props
item.description: Notifications on the CB have a fifth switch, When somebody gives me props. Until now, props people gave you waited in Profile until you happened to open it, because nothing on the radio lights up for them. Switch it on and the device is told when somebody gives you props, with who wrote them and, unless you switched the words off, how they start. It is off until you switch it on, like every switch there. Pressing it opens Profile at Your props, on the street, with the radio switched on for that page so you can Confirm or Reject them straight away. Only a claimed username has props, so only a device switched on as one is told. It never says how many are waiting, and whoever wrote the props is never told anything: not whether you were notified, nor whether you read, confirmed or rejected what they wrote. Show the words of a message is now Show the words of a message, a post or props, because it covers all three. Privacy and the CB guide say all of it.

item.title: Props on your profile
item.description: Every profile on the CB has a Props tab, for props: a sentence or a short paragraph thanking somebody, acknowledging them or celebrating them, usually for something they did for you or for the community. Open somebody’s profile, from their handle on the channel or their name on Who’s online, and the Props tab shows the props they have been given, newest first, each with who wrote it, and a box to give them some of your own. Nothing goes up until its person says yes. Props you are given wait in Your props, in Profile on the radio, where Confirm puts one on your Props tab and Reject deletes it. Nobody is told it was rejected. What you wrote for somebody waits on their tab where only you and they can read it, with Take it back, and one of yours waits for each person at a time. Your Props tab is shut until you open it, with Show my props on the CB in Profile, like your pets, avatars and chimeras. While it is shut nobody can give you props and your tab shows none; what you confirmed comes back when you open it again. Giving props and having a Props tab both need a claimed username, because a prop carries a name on somebody else’s profile. You can take any prop off your tab, whoever wrote one can take it back, and a moderator can take one down. Nothing counts props, and nothing says when one was written. Forget me and Delete my account delete yours. Privacy and the CB guide say all of it, and Props & Gratitude in the forums is still there for thanks the whole community reads.

item.title: Edit your messages on the CB
item.description: A message you sent on the CB can be edited. Edit is under its three dots, beside Copy and Take off, and opens the words in a box where they were: Enter saves and Escape leaves it as it was. ↑ in an empty message box edits your newest message, the way chat does. Only the words change. The message keeps its picture, sticker and reactions, says edited and when beside its time on every radio, and still goes 48 hours after you first sent it. The words it had before are not kept anywhere. Only whoever sent a message can edit it. A moderator can take any message off the air, and edit only their own: taking words down and putting words in somebody’s mouth are not the same thing. A message marked CLAIMED edits only with that username’s own password, and one marked BASE only for the base. An edit tells nobody unless it @mentions somebody it did not name before, and then only them. A message taken to the forums after it was edited says edited there too. Privacy and the CB guide say all of it.

item.title: Pictures send from an iPhone
item.description: A picture sent on the CB from an iPhone was refused every time, with the radio saying it still carried its camera data. It did not: the radio redraws every picture before it goes, but the way Safari and every other iPhone browser save a redrawn picture writes a small block of their own into it, saying its size and colour space, and this site refuses any picture carrying that kind of block. The radio now takes that block off too, so a picture from an iPhone, or from Safari on a Mac, goes. The same fix reaches pictures on the Brass Tacks Board and in the forums. This site now also refuses a picture still carrying a Photoshop block, where a photo app can write the name of a place, and the radio takes that off as well.

item.title: The forums take pictures, files and @mentions, and six more categories
item.description: The forums have three new categories in Community: Discourse, for the news, ideas and arguments of the day; Pets; and Props & Gratitude, for thanking somebody out loud. And three in Staff, for the directors and the board: Back Office Operations, Grantmaking and Finance. As in every staff category but the Town Hall’s Executive Session, an administrator can read them too. A post can carry pictures and files. This reverses what the forums said when they opened this morning, that they take words only. A picture is redrawn in your own browser before it goes, by the same code the CB uses, which takes off what a camera wrote into it, where it was taken first of all, and you can say what is in it. A file can be a PDF, plain text, Markdown, CSV, RTF, a Word, Excel, PowerPoint or OpenDocument document, or an EPUB, up to 5 MB, and is checked against what it says it is: never a web page, a script, an SVG or a document with macros. Neither has a public address. Each is fetched with your pass by people who can read its topic, a file is only ever saved to your device, and both go when their post does. @mentions. This reverses “the forums send no notifications”. Typing @ offers the people in the topic and anybody claimed on Who’s online; a mention shows as the person’s name, which opens their profile, and MENTIONS YOU marks a post that names you. Mentions, beside Latest, lists where somebody has mentioned you, worked out each time you look and kept nowhere. A mention tells a device only if When somebody @mentions me is switched on there, and only if that claimed username can read the category. Search reads file names and what pictures are said to show. The privacy page, the CB guide and Architecture say all of it.

item.title: The CB keeps fifty messages, for 48 hours each
item.description: Every channel on the CB now keeps its latest fifty messages, and each one stays for 48 hours after it was sent, rather than ten messages gone at midnight in Colorado. People on the street live in timezones all over the world, and a channel cleared at one city’s midnight was clearing in the middle of somebody else’s afternoon, so anybody asleep through a conversation never saw it. World, every room’s channel and every place on the Slake keep the same rule. Everything said before tonight’s midnight in Colorado still goes at that midnight, as it was promised when it was sent. The 48 hours start with what is sent after it. A message from before today says which day beside its time on the radio, yesterday or the day’s name, in your own day, and so does a room’s last busy time in the World room. A forum topic made from messages on more than one day dates each of them. The privacy page says so, and so do the CB guide, the Community Center’s house norms and the forums, which are now for what needs longer than two days.

item.title: Ten more animals on Chimera Obscura’s shelf
item.description: A pig, a porcupine, a fox, a cat, a dog, an elephant, a penguin, an owl, a turtle and a zebra are on the shelf at Chimera Obscura, and every part of each fits every body: wings, flippers, hooves, talons and paddling feet, a snout, a beak and a trunk with tusks, floppy ears, big fan ears and ear tufts, a porcupine’s quills, a turtle’s shell and a zebra’s mane, and stripes, a tuxedo, a facial disc and a patch over one eye. Arms and feet are parts of their own now, so a bear can have a penguin’s flippers and an owl’s talons. Every chimera kept in a Profile and every link made before keeps its own arms and feet and opens just as it did. A pig with a porcupine’s parts is a Porkypine, the name Randimals and Stimpunks made together, now that both animals are here.

item.title: Chimeras kept in Profile, named, shown and sent as stickers
item.description: Keep it in my Profile, on Chimera Obscura’s bench, signed on to the CB, keeps the chimera on the table with its name. In Profile on the radio, Your chimeras lists them, each with which animal gave which part: rename one, put it back on the table to change it, download its picture, or delete it. Sticker on the radio sends one of your chimeras to the channel, with its name and its parts in words. With a claimed username, Show my chimeras on the CB puts them in a new Chimeras tab in your profile. It starts off. What is kept is which animal gave each part and the name, never a picture and nothing about when, under your scrambled handle; Forget me and Delete my account delete them. The privacy page has a section on it. Chimeras are drawn as elements now, wherever they appear, and on the radio on the table’s own white.

item.title: Chimera Obscura opens on the street
item.description: A camera obscura between The Sandbox and Your Room, painted black inside, where a lens in the roof throws a chimera onto a round white table: one creature made out of two animals, the body from one and the head, ears, mouth, tail, back, colours and markings from either, or from any animal on the shelf. It opens on an otteraccoon, the request it began with. The shelf has a bear, a mouse, a panda, an armadillo, a rabbit, a badger, an otter and a raccoon, every part drawn as code and fitted to whatever body it lands on. Name your chimera, toss for one, or copy a link that carries it after the # in the address. An animal the shelf does not have yet is asked for in the suggestion box, which now opens filled in when you arrive from the room, and gets drawn for everybody. Nothing in the room calls an AI. Bearmouse, Pandillo and Bunnybadger hang on its wall: Ryan’s, Chelsea’s and Inna’s chimeras, drawn by Becky Hicks for stimpunks.org’s About page and here under CC BY-SA 4.0 with her yes. Our friends at Randimals make combined animals as plush toys; no name the room suggests is one of their characters, and the Porkypine is a name they and Stimpunks made together. Also: a job for the Adventurer’s Guild, a slot on the Community Center’s service board for asking for an animal, the room’s own faces, Gilda Display and Gantari, and a line in How it’s made saying the three on the wall are Becky’s and drawn by hand.

item.title: A book of the Reading Room’s records on the yurt’s Bookshelf
item.description: The Faery Yurt’s Bookshelf has a book now, at Helen’s ask, listing what plays on the gramophone in the Reading Room: her Library Music playlist, a song to a line with its runtime, bound like the Music Room’s books under the yurt’s gramophone and with the playlist’s name on the cover. Each line goes to that record on the Reading Room’s shelf, and nothing in the book plays. It stands above the door through to the Reading Room. Written by make-yurt-yarn.py from data/yurt-yarn.json, like the other books; changed: faery-yurt.html, love.css (§14), tools/make-yurt-yarn.py.

item.title: The profile card editor asks before it throws changes away
item.description: A press outside the editor, Escape or Cancel no longer throws away changes you have not saved. If anything has changed since you opened your card or last saved it, the editor asks first: Save and close, Close without saving or Keep editing. With nothing changed, it closes as it always did. Clear my card now clears the frame and the effect too, and after saving, the keyboard goes back to Edit my profile card. Changed: cb.js, cb-guide.html.

item.title: The yarn plays in the Music Room, and the yurt keeps a songbook
item.description: Helen’s playlist, Faery Yurt’s Yarn, was read again, at her ask: she has added a great deal to it since 2026-10-13, and every song on it now stands in the record case in the Music Room, in the playlist’s own order, each with its runtime, with the whole yarn on the phonograph above them, one press, running until you stop it. The upload that had replaced AURORA’s dead copy is off the data, because the playlist no longer carries the dead copy. A second playlist of hers, Strange things will happen, is in the Music Room beside it, at her ask the same afternoon: its own plate on the phonograph and its own shelf of records. One upload on the yarn has embedding switched off by its channel, so its sleeve is a door to YouTube and says so, rather than a frame showing a refusal. The music plays in the Music Room and nowhere else now. Helen’s call, reversing her own arrangement of 2026-10-13: in the yurt the deck and the record case have gone through the door, and under the phonograph there is a songbook instead, bound like Nature Notes, listing every song on the yarn a line at a time with its runtime; each line goes to that record in the Music Room. Nothing on the yurt’s own page plays the yarn, and make-yurt-yarn.py refuses it if anything does. The phonograph stays, and its record still turns at MAX GLITTER. yurt-notebook.js binds every book on the page now, not only the first. Changed: data/yurt-yarn.json, tools/make-yurt-yarn.py, yurt-notebook.js, faery-yurt.html, faery-music-room.html, love.css (§14), liner-notes.html, DECISIONS.md, the poster’s lines for both rooms. The yurt has a book per playlist now, each with its playlist’s name on the cover, at her ask later the same afternoon; the lines still go to the records in the Music Room. And the Reading Room has a gramophone, at her ask: her Library Music playlist on it, switched on from its plate and off from the way back under it, and every song on it as a record on a shelf among the bookcases, the Music Room’s case in that room’s own clothes. The dial’s line there says MAX turns the record. rack.js grew an opt-in, data-rack-switch, which shows a screen’s way back once its own plate is pressed; no other room’s screen takes it. Changed as well: faery-reading-room.html, love.css (§114), rack.js.

item.title: Notifications for the CB
item.description: The CB can notify you now, even with the site closed, after several requests from our community and especially our staff, as more of our chat and work moves onto the street. Notifications, under Your radio, switches a device on for any of four things, each off until you switch it on: somebody @mentioning you, a message in a room you follow, a call starting in a room you follow or the World call, and every message on World. A notification shows who and where and the start of the message, unless you switch the words off; a call’s says only that it has started, never who is in it. Pressing one opens its room. This reverses the CB’s “no alerts”, Ryan’s call, and Privacy, the Community Center and the CB guide say so. The radio itself still has no chime, no badge and no unread count, and still listens only while it is open. What is kept is one record per device: its push address, the handle and a scrambled form of the pass it was switched on with, and what it chose; nothing it is sent. Notifications travel through your browser’s own push service, encrypted so that service cannot read them. A private room tells only people who can hear it, a changed password stops a device at once, and signing off, Forget me and deleting your username switch it off. Changed: cb.js, cb.css, netlify/cb/lib.mjs, two functions, privacy.html, cb-guide.html, community-center.html; new: cb-sw.js, netlify/functions/cb-push.mjs, tools/check-push.py.

item.title: The World room: every room on the street, and who is in each
item.description: The World room is open, Ryan’s brief, past the Garden: knowledge gardens and our garden spider, webs connecting gardens around the world. The spider has strung a web between every room on the street, caught by the dawn, and every room is a garden on it, in a bed for each part of the Map. Anybody can read the list. Signed on to the CB, it shows which rooms are active now: who has chosen Be seen here in each, which have somebody in their call, and when each was last busy today. Show every room, the active ones or the quiet ones, and put them in the street’s order, latest activity first, or most active first. Privacy says what it shows, including the one thing it shows that was not shown before: when a room’s channel last had a message. Most active reverses the street’s no-headcount rule for this one order, Ryan’s call: the server counts the people seen in each room and in its call each time somebody asks, and sends the order and never the numbers. It is the one place the street counts people, and the Mission now says so. The World room’s own channel is the World channel, and its own call is the World call, so there is no second channel or call to split people between. This reverses the rule that no page may be called world.html, which only existed so a room’s call could not collide with the World’s. Changed: cb.js, netlify/cb/lib.mjs, tools/make-sitemap.py, community-center.html, privacy.html, mission.html, cb-guide.html. New: world.html, world.js, netlify/functions/cb-world.mjs, tools/make-world.py, and §119 in love.css, which moves the small screens and print to §120 and §121.

item.title: Getting started at the Community Center, and no more meeting hall
item.description: Our community uses Stimpunks.World and its forums for everything now, Ryan’s call, so the Community Center no longer mentions Stoat or Discord. This reverses the meeting hall of 2026-09-29, which sent people to our Stoat server for anything worth keeping and for the CB’s password. The room opens with Getting started in the community, from Ryan’s draft: ask to join on the Stimpunks Community page, which gives you a starter password; sign on to the CB with it; claim your username with a password of your own, step by step on the radio’s own buttons; and then some quests to go on, from an introduction in the forums to adopting a pet, collecting badges and patches, and making your profile your own. The starter password is the community password by a friendlier name: the radio and the CB guide still call it that, and the room says so. Every page that said to ask for it in the meeting hall now points at Getting started: the guest bar on the radio, the CB guide, the suggestion box in The Sandbox, the Fishbowl’s call, and the privacy page. Changed: community-center.html, guest.js, cb-guide.html, privacy.html, data/sandbox.json, tools/make-town-hall.py, liner-notes.html.

item.title: Coping in the forums, a week at a time
item.description: Coping is a category in the forums now, Ryan’s call, because it is one of the busiest channels on our Discord and people moving over need somewhere to go. A topic there goes a week after its last post, where Discord keeps that channel for ever: a place for the hard days is not somewhere to keep them. Like every category, only claimed usernames on the CB can read it. Changed: data/forum.json, netlify/cb/lib.mjs, tools/make-forum.py, which now refuses a longer keep for it.

item.title: The forums, for what needs longer than the CB’s day
item.description: The forums are open: topics in categories, after Discourse, for conversations that need to last longer than the channel’s midnight, Ryan’s brief. The categories follow our Discord and Stoat’s channels: Announcements, Introductions, a Help desk, the Watering hole, Events, Mutual aid, Show your work, Work opportunities, Infodumps, Reading and watching, Education, Science and making, Nature, Artificial Intelligence, Operations and Editorial, and staff areas for our moderators, directors and board, by the same CB roles as the Town Hall’s rooms. The hope is that the CB and the forums together let us leave Discord and Stoat. Only a claimed username can read them, and a category somebody’s roles do not reach is never sent to them. Each category says how long a topic stays after its last post, a week, three months, six months or for good, and each topic says the date it goes; three months is the default. A pinned topic stays while it is pinned. Markdown, replies, quotes, reactions named and never counted, editing and taking down your own posts, search, and for moderators pin, close, move and take down. No notifications, no badges, no counts, and nothing kept about who reads: what is new to you is worked out in your own browser. A link on a line of its own becomes a preview: our server reads the page once, when the post is made, for its title and description, from public addresses only and with no pictures; a YouTube video becomes a press-to-play button that says how long it runs; a room on the street shows its own name. Take to the forums, under a message’s three dots on the radio, starts a topic with messages ticked off the channel. Our server copies them off the channel itself, exactly as they were sent, and whoever sent one can take it back out of the topic. The house norm now says to ask everybody first, as for a screenshot. They wear the CB’s themes: your radio’s, or any of them chosen for the forums alone, with its colours, its face for headings and its drawing. Privacy says what they keep, and the CB guide how they work. New: forum.html, forum.js, forum.css, netlify/functions/cb-forum.mjs, data/forum.json, tools/make-forum.py. Changed: netlify/cb/lib.mjs, cb.js, cb.css, privacy.html, community-center.html, architecture.html.

item.title: Otters in the kelp: an effect, a theme, a frame and a decoration
item.description: A large, cute profile effect, Otters in the kelp, Ryan’s ask. Over the card’s banner, sunlit kelp rises to the surface with its floats and light falls through the water. One sea otter floats on its back with a strand of kelp across it and a shell on its chest. Another rolls over at the surface now and then, and a third swims back and forth below, trailing bubbles, over urchins and a starfish. Bubbles rise across the whole profile. When the profile opens, and once a minute, the kelp forest grows up through the whole profile, and a big otter swims up, rolls once, floats with its eyes shut and drifts away. A Kelp Forest radio theme, in deep green water, foam, sea glass and the kelp’s sunlit gold, with the radio’s name in a round, friendly face, and kelp, bubbles, light and now and then a floating otter along its trims. Every word clears 4.5 to 1. It is a banner and a nameplate for profiles too. With it come a Kelp fronds frame, with floats, bubbles, starfish and scallops, and an Otters in kelp decoration, two little otters floating at the foot of a ring of kelp, both drawn in the card’s own colours. It is after the Arcade’s Otterly Adorbs, and so after Helen Edgar’s Stimpunks Solidarity and Otters and Star Stuff’s zine No. 58, The Stone You Keep, and it keeps the cabinet’s rules: floating fills nothing, no otter is ranked, the kelp does the holding, nobody holds paws, and nobody keeps a stone in a pouch. The tools refuse each of those. Like every effect, it moves only at MAX GLITTER or after Let my theme move, and nothing flashes. The liner notes and the CB guide say so. Changed: profile.js, cb-themes.js, call.js, cb.css, love.css, netlify/cb/lib.mjs, tools/make-profile.py, tools/check-contrast.py, cb-guide.html, liner-notes.html.

item.title: A Halloween theme, frame and decoration, to pair with the Lagoon
item.description: Black Leather Lagoon is a radio theme now, in the street’s Lagoon’s own colours: black water, the screen’s bone, acid green and poster red, with the radio’s name in its dripping bill face. Along its trims, its dividers and down its sides there is a drive-in screen glowing over the water now and then, and reeds with cattails, and bats. It is a banner and a nameplate for profiles too. Every word in it clears 4.5 to 1, and like the room nothing in it flickers. A Graveyard gate frame: iron railings with spear tips round all four sides, cobwebs in the corners, and a spider letting itself down from each top corner. A Jack-o’-lanterns decoration: a pumpkin vine round the avatar you wear, with lanterns whose carved faces glow, and two bats. Both are drawn in the card’s own theme, so in the Lagoon’s the pumpkins are its poster red and the light in them its acid green. Together with the Black Leather Lagoon effect, the four make one Halloween profile, Ryan’s ask. Nobody real is drawn in any of them; the liner notes say whose world it is. Changed: call.js, cb-themes.js, cb.css, love.css, profile.js, netlify/cb/lib.mjs, tools/check-contrast.py, cb-guide.html, liner-notes.html.

item.title: The Lagoon effect rears up when a profile opens
item.description: The Black Leather Lagoon effect now plays across the whole profile when it opens, the way Discord’s do, and then once a minute while it is open. Black water rises across the foot of the profile, mist climbs off it, the sea serpent’s coils break the surface, its head rears up over the profile and looks about with a flick of its tongue, and a flurry of bats bursts out past it. Then it all sinks back, after about nine seconds. The scene in the banner carries on the whole time. Ryan’s ask. It crosses the words, so it is there only where drawings move, at MAX GLITTER or after Let my theme move, like every effect’s pass, and every fade in it takes a second or more, so nothing flashes. Changing something else in Edit my profile card no longer starts an effect over. The CB guide says so. Changed: profile.js, cb.css, cb.js, tools/make-profile.py, cb-guide.html.

item.title: Black Leather Lagoon, a profile effect
item.description: A detailed profile effect after the street’s Black Leather Lagoon and The Cramps, Ryan’s ask. Over the card’s banner, a drive-in screen stands in black water with a giant bloodshot eye looking about on it, its glow breathing slowly. A sea serpent of our own rises and sinks in front of it, with its eyes on stalks and pondweed on its head. There are reeds, a lobby card on a post in the shallows, and the screen rippling in the water. Poison ivy creeps down both sides of the profile, leopard print runs along the foot, a finned hot rod is parked in the corner, and from time to time bats fly across the whole profile from the screen’s side. Their world, not them, Ryan’s call: nobody real is drawn, and nothing of the band’s is used. The card carries a credit naming The Cramps, Lux Interior and Poison Ivy, and the poison ivy is a nod to her name. It is the one effect drawn in its room’s own colours rather than the card’s theme, and, like the room, nothing in it flickers. It moves only at MAX GLITTER or after Let my theme move, as every effect does. The liner notes and the CB guide say so. Changed: profile.js, cb.js, cb.css, netlify/cb/lib.mjs, tools/make-profile.py, cb-guide.html, liner-notes.html.

item.title: A profile lists the patches on its jacket
item.description: The Battle jacket tab in somebody’s profile lists every patch sewn on, under the jacket, in the street’s order: each patch drawn on its own, its name, and the room it came from, linked to where it lies, so you can go and find one. A screen reader hears what each patch looks like. Ryan’s ask. Nothing is counted. Links in a profile’s tabs are the panel’s amber now. They were the browser’s own default blue, a colour nobody chose, which the job links in the Badges and jobs tab had been since profiles opened. The CB guide says so. Changed: cb.js, cb.css, cb-guide.html.

item.title: Frames and effects for profiles on the CB
item.description: A profile card can have a frame and an effect now, after Discord’s. A frame is a band of your card’s theme round all four sides of your profile, outside it: briar, ivy, brass and rivets, fairy lights, a stitched patch, a film strip, a circuit board, crystals, a flower garland or a starry night. An effect is drawn over your profile: butterflies, fireflies, falling petals or leaves, snow, bubbles, sparkles, shooting stars, music notes or hearts. Part of it stays along the edges and in the banner, and the rest crosses the whole profile from time to time. Both are in Edit my profile card, and both are drawn only in your card’s own colours. An effect’s pass crosses the words, Ryan’s call, which is the one place the radio lets a drawing do that. So it is drawn only where the radio’s drawings move, at MAX GLITTER or after Let my theme move: a profile standing still has nothing on its words, and nothing in an effect flashes. The CB guide and privacy say so. Changed: profile.js, cb.js, cb.css, netlify/cb/lib.mjs, tools/make-profile.py, cb-guide.html, community-center.html, privacy.html.

item.title: A moderator can clear one profile card
item.description: The moderators’ desk can clear somebody’s profile card without deleting their username. Until now a card that broke our covenant could only go with the whole username, its password, pets, avatars, jobs and patches. Looking a username up at the desk now says whether it has a card, and Clear their profile card, which asks once more, takes the card and its nameplate on Who’s online exactly as Clear my card does. Everything else stays, and they can fill in a new one. Ryan’s call. Nothing is kept about it: not who cleared a card, not when, not what it said, and the accounts checker refuses one that would. The desk still leaves a moderator’s username alone, card included. Privacy, the CB guide and the Moderators’ room say so. Changed: desk.js, netlify/cb/lib.mjs, netlify/functions/cb-account-admin.mjs, tools/make-accounts.py, privacy.html, cb-guide.html, town-hall-moderators.html.

item.title: Profile cards on the CB
item.description: Pressing a handle opens a whole profile now, over the page, after requests for profiles more like Discord’s. On the left is the person’s card; on the right, where Discord has Board, Activity and Wishlist, are tabs for their Avatars, Pets, Badges and jobs and Battle jacket, each shown as they have chosen. A name on Who’s online opens the same profile. The CB guide says how it works. A claimed username can fill in its card, at Edit my profile card in Profile, with the card drawn beside the choices as they change: a theme from the radio’s own, a banner from their drawings, a decoration round the avatar you wear (flowers, ivy, stars, gears, flames, moons and more, drawn in the card’s own colours), a face for your name from the street’s typefaces, a nameplate under your name on Who’s online, your pronouns, a few words about you, up to five links elsewhere, each shown with its site after it, and your favourite room on the street, with a line on why. Ryan’s calls: whatever you fill in is shown to anybody signed on to the CB, as the avatar you wear is, with no switch; and no card says when anybody joined, because a date beside a name invites ranking who has been here longest. Every colour on a card is a pair the contrast checker already holds for every theme, and every drawing on it moves only where the radio’s do. Clear my card, Forget me and deleting the username delete it. Privacy has the whole of what is kept. Changed: cb.js, cb.css, love.css, netlify/cb/lib.mjs, privacy.html, cb-guide.html, community-center.html; new: profile.js, tools/make-profile.py, two functions.

item.title: Small is one press away on the CB
item.description: The radio’s bar has − and + where Size was: one press goes from Large to Normal to Small, or back up, with no choice to open first. Each button says which size it goes to, and says so when the radio is already as small or as large as it goes. Ryan’s ask: getting to Small was a step too much. Move is six dots now, to drag by, or to press and then use the arrow keys, as before. The bar still fits on one row in every theme. The CB guide and the Community Center say so. Changed: cb.js, cb.css, cb-guide.html, community-center.html.

item.title: Ryan’s favourite games, as themes for the CB
item.description: Another group under the radio’s Themes: Ryan’s favourite games: Castle Crashers, Dragon Age: Inquisition, Metroid, Mega Man, Fable III, Skyrim, Doom, Portal, The Witcher 3, Grand Theft Auto V, The Legend of Zelda and Shadow of Mordor. Each has its game’s palette, a shape after it and a drawing under the bar, along the foot, along the dividers and down the sides: cartoon castles with pennants flying, green rifts glowing and gold filigree, blue cavern rock and round doors, an energy meter filling and ladders, a golden trail twinkling over cobbles, snowy peaks under an aurora with snow falling, riveted metal over slime with fire that glows and never flickers, white panels with a blue portal and an orange one, dark pines under a moon with mist drifting, a sunset with palms swaying, the overworld’s trees and water, and, for Shadow of Mordor, rune medallions after the game’s runes, gold rings with marks glowing in them, over black mountains and lava with ash drifting. Each rune’s mark is made up here, and none is the game’s or a letter of Tolkien’s. No character, logo, emblem or symbol of any game is drawn, and each game’s studio and the owner of its trade mark are named on the radio’s line when you choose it, and in the CB guide and the liner notes. Every word still clears 4.5 to 1. Changed: love.css, cb.css, cb.js, call.js, cb-themes.js, tools/check-contrast.py.

item.title: GeoCities pages for the CB
item.description: Another group under the radio’s Themes: GeoCities pages, Ryan’s picks from Restorativland’s GeoCities archive: Divine Louise Brooks, Paula’s Page, Shop Til U Drop!, mansnhomepage, Double U for W, Beatnik Termites, The Green Room and Sarah’s Room. Each has its page’s colours, a shape after it and a drawing of its own under the bar, along the foot, along the dividers and down the sides: blocks and a black swoosh, bamboo and ferns and a lizard, neon checks and zebra stripes and shopping bags, pastel checks and sunflowers, chalk scribbles, chain links and doodled guitars, olive table columns, and a starry sky with a column of rainbow stars. Each page is credited as it names its maker, and by its title and address where it names nobody, on the radio’s line and in the CB guide and the liner notes. Nothing on the pages is used, nobody on them is drawn, and no email address or detail about anybody is repeated. Every word still clears 4.5 to 1. Changed: love.css, cb.css, cb.js, call.js, cb-themes.js, tools/check-contrast.py.

item.title: Winamp skins for the CB
item.description: A new group under the radio’s Themes: Winamp skins, Ryan’s picks from the Winamp Skin Museum: Zelda Amp, Microchip, ASCII-Amp, Super Mario Land Amp, Dig Dug Amp, deviantAMP, HP 49G, Winamp Mario, The Cube, Pip-Boy 3000, Game Boy and TI-82. Each has its skin’s colours, a shape after it (hard pixel corners, dashed ASCII edges, calculator keys, the Game Boy’s one round corner) and a drawing of its own under the bar, along the foot, along the dividers and down the sides: hearts and hedges, a circuit board, typed characters, pyramids and pipes, the layers of earth, sliders, keys, bricks and coins, green cubes, a gauge, a cross pad, and a graph drawing itself. Each skin’s maker is named as its own readme names them, on the radio’s line when you choose it and in the CB guide and the liner notes, and where a readme names nobody, it says so. No skin’s bitmap is used, and nothing from the games and machines the skins were after is drawn. Every word still clears 4.5 to 1. Changed: love.css, cb.css, cb.js, call.js, cb-themes.js, tools/check-contrast.py.

item.title: The CB’s worlds go down the sides and along the dividers
item.description: A world’s drawing now runs down both sides of the radio, just outside it, and along every divider between its parts, Ryan’s ask: ivy climbing, LCARS’ columns, a spine, tubing, stars, sparkles, sunflowers, greebles, rainbow and ink. Each side stands on a narrow rail of the theme’s own colour, so the drawing shows whatever room is behind the radio, and the radio keeps a little further from the edge of the window to make room for them. On a window as narrow as a phone the sides are left off. Nothing starts again when a message arrives. The sides are drawn once, longer than the radio can grow, and the radio shows as much of them as it is tall. They move only where the rest of the drawing does: at MAX GLITTER, or after Let my theme move. The CB guide says so. Changed: cb-themes.js, cb.css, cb.js, call.js.

item.title: Worlds for the CB: themes with drawings
item.description: The radio’s Colours are Themes now, and there are a lot more of them, Ryan’s list: Solarized dark and Solarized light, and worlds that have nothing to do with radios, Biophilic, Star Stuff, LCARS, Max Glitter, Solarpunk, Biomechanical, Greeble, Crip Cyborg, Unicorn Poop and Wabi-sabi. Each world has a drawing under the radio’s bar and along its foot, its own corners and borders, and its own lettering for the radio’s name and headings: ivy and mushrooms, stars and a ringed planet, LCARS’ elbow and pills, sparkles, sunflowers and a solar panel, a spine, a plate of greebles, a CPAP hose and oxygen on a rack, rainbow swirls, and a crack mended in gold. The drawings move at MAX GLITTER, growing, twinkling, glowing or breathing, and stand still at the other settings unless you press Let my theme move, under the themes. Nothing in any of them flashes, and nothing on the radio moves when a message arrives. Solarized and Wabi-sabi never move at all. Every word still clears 4.5 to 1 in every theme, and every sentence stays in the radio’s own easy-to-read type: a theme’s lettering is for its name and headings only. What each world is after is on the radio’s line when you choose it, and in the CB guide and the liner notes. Changed: love.css, cb.css, cb.js, call.js, the new cb-themes.js, tools/check-contrast.py.

item.title: Colour schemes for the CB
item.description: The radio comes in colour schemes now, from a request: Colours, under Your radio on the CB, offers Amber, which it has always been, Daylight, dark on a pale case, High contrast, black, white and yellow, and three faceplates, Green screen, Red readout and Teal glow. Each shows a little picture of itself, and the call window wears the same. Your radio remembers which, like its size. Everybody starts on Match my device, so the radio looks different now for some people: High contrast if your device asks for more contrast, Daylight if it is set to light, and Amber otherwise, changing when your device does. The bar you see before you sign on follows your device the same way. Every scheme keeps every word at least 4.5 to 1 against what it sits on, and High contrast at 7 to 1, and the site’s contrast checker holds each one. The CB guide and the privacy page say so. Changed: love.css, cb.css, cb.js, call.js, guest.js, tools/check-contrast.py.

item.title: Follow puts a rack’s film on the screen
item.description: On a rack, Enter now puts the film up on the room’s screen. Follow, Catch up and a spot from the CB said to press Enter, and Enter played the film small in its card under the screen, which was confusing, at Ryan’s report. Now the keyboard goes on the card’s button for the screen, and the film starts on the screen from where the host is. Anything that is not on a rack is as it was. A film plays in one place at a time. Putting a card’s film up on the screen stops it in its card, and playing it in its card takes it off the screen, so the same film no longer plays twice, out of step. Another card playing in its own place is left alone. The CB guide says so. Changed: cb.js, rack.js.

item.title: Watching a live video together on the CB
item.description: Add my spot and Host this film now come up for a live video too, at Ryan’s ask, so the channel can be told when one is being screened. Until now Watching together left live videos out, because a time means nothing in one. A live video’s spot is @live: Add my spot writes @live in “the video” at #the-room, and pressing @live gets that video’s play button ready on your page, or says it is already playing. It presses nothing, and the room’s link in the message gets it ready when you arrive. Hosting one says it is live instead of giving a place. Beside the host, Catch up gets the video’s play button ready, and there is no Follow, because there is nothing in a live video to keep in step. A moderator’s live video put up from Screen a video says on everybody else’s screen that it runs until you stop it. The CB guide and the privacy page say so. Changed: love-embed.js, cb.js, netlify/cb/lib.mjs and its tests, cb-beacon.mjs, and the sets in hermitage.js, looming.js and rave.js.

item.title: Quieter messages on the CB
item.description: The words Copy, React and Take off are off every message on the CB, from a proposal Ryan brought: a row of buttons on every message was a lot to look at. At the end of each message’s line there are two small icons now, a smiley for React and three dots for More, which opens Copy and Take off under the line. They show while your pointer is on the message or the keyboard is in it, and always on a phone or tablet, which has nothing to point with. Out of sight they are still in their place, so Tab reaches them, a screen reader names them, and nothing on the line moves when they come and go. The CB guide says so. Changed: cb.js, cb.css.

item.title: A fairy door at the foot of the Bough House’s tree
item.description: A fairy door at the foot of the trunk in the Bough House, at Helen’s ask: arched in the room’s own rust, with a round window, a gold knob, a step and a toadstool beside it, the fallen leaves lying round it, and the lede says so (its first version was too small to see, and grew the same day). Nothing moves; the share card carries it because it lifts the drawing whole.

item.title: The Emergent Future Worlds Meets Mountain Man, David’s cabin at the summit over the campgrounds
item.description: A new home on the campgrounds, and the first off the main campsite: The Emergent Future Worlds Meets Mountain Man, David’s, a log cabin at the top of the mountain that stands over the field, from his brief as Helen passed it on, by the name she gave; he is David Gray-Hammond, he/they, and his own photograph, with the Diversity Power List honours in front of the NeuroHub wall, is framed in Whose this is with its record. Inside, at night: a fire behind the glass of the stove, with the coffee pot on top and a shelf of cups; LED strips along the walls in a colour you pick; a corner sofa, a high-back sofa and two high-back armchairs round a table with the crisps, the sweets and a bowl of rainbow sweets, bright cushions on every seat and bright bean bags on the floor; a big screen with Future Mountain Man, his own playlist, put on whole in his order and every video on it one press each under it; a speaker either side; an oil diffuser; one wolf asleep on the rug. Through the window, the whole back wall: a lake under a full moon, the pack on the warm ground outside, and the hot spring’s steam. One switch runs the cabin: the fire, the strips, the diffuser, the big screen’s plate and the speakers go on and off together, saying so in words, remembering nothing. The cabin is drawn on and still; from the switch’s press the fire burns and the wisps rise, at Regular and MAX, and at Gentle they stay lit and still. Next colour steps the strips through the cabin’s colours and then the whole rainbow; at MAX a second button lets them drift round it, slowly, until you stop them, and nothing flashes. Change the scent steps the diffuser through its shelf of oils, lavender to cupcakes, saying which is in and never what it does. Hear the wolves howl makes the pack howl for about five seconds, out of the browser’s own oscillators and no recording; beside it, at Helen’s ask, a recording of real wolves from Wikimedia Commons, made by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and in the public domain, played from Commons by its own address when pressed and never hosted here. The cushions wear whichever colour the strips are, and change with them, Helen’s ask too. The window opens onto David’s own photographs of Lake Geneva, taken at Lausanne in July 2026 and sent by Helen on his behalf the same day: nobody in them, described in our words, each with its record in the polaroid file and its file stripped of metadata, to scroll through one at a time. It runs on the mountain’s own heat. A hot spring steams in a ring of stones outside the door, with a shelf of rock to sit on and a step a wheelchair transfers from; the spring’s water runs under the floor and a small geothermal plant behind the cabin makes the electricity. Ryan’s Solarpunk Hermitage runs on the sun; this runs on the ground. Beside the spring’s words, two photographs of springs like it, Fabio Sasso’s and Jeremy Mowery’s on Unsplash, chosen by Helen, credited and linked; the second has three people far off on a boardwalk, strangers to the street, and the caption says so, Helen’s call. A cable car goes up from the pond, level with the platform at both ends so a wheelchair rolls straight on: it is how Ryan, Helen and Jess visit. It hangs on its wire down the left-hand edge of the page, at Helen’s ask: Send the cable car runs it up and down the wire and stops it, it stays still until sent and at Gentle, and pressing the car takes you back down to the campsite. On the campgrounds’ board its sign stands first, and its light is the sixth: one lit window so far above the field it sits among the stars. On the map the mountain is one card folded to a point over the field. The neighbours line in every home on the campgrounds names it, and its own names them. tools/make-mountain-cabin.py writes the screen, the rack, the wall, the window and the credits from data/mountain-cabin.json, requires a runtime on every video and refuses one on the playlist, refuses a photograph with no record, holds mountain-man.js to storing nothing, sending nothing and howling no louder than a ceiling, and sweeps the room’s voice for a cure, a conquest and a wolf drawn as a threat. A job marker (a carabiner), a share card, a fractal in the room’s own colours, Now Playing, the liner notes. Staatliches and Assistant arrive on the street. love.css: section 118 is the room; small screens and print move to 119 and 120, with every reference.

item.title: The hundred points in the CB’s quick reactions
item.description: 💯 is in the quick row that React opens on the CB, after the crying face. Ryan’s ask. It shows who pressed it, like every reaction, and never how many. Changed: netlify/cb/lib.mjs, cb.js and the CB guide.

item.title: The leaves fall in the Bough House, when you ask
item.description: A button under the Bough House’s drawing lets the autumn leaves fall, at Helen’s ask: they let go of the crown, drift down swinging and turning, and land among the others at the foot of the ladder. The same button stops them, and stopping clears the air at once. Nothing falls until somebody presses, at any setting, and the dial never starts it.

item.title: A hammock and a platform swing by the pond
item.description: By the pond between the pitches, at Helen’s ask: a hammock strung between two posts, and one of the swing seats is now a platform swing, wide and railed at each end, that a wheelchair can roll straight onto.

item.title: The Bough House, Jess’s tree house at pitch 05, and the pond between it and the Faery Yurt
item.description: A new pitch on the campgrounds, next to the Faery Yurt: the Bough House, Jess’s, from her brief as Helen passed it on. A tree house up in an autumn grove, built round the tree, so the trunk comes up through the floor and out of the roof and two of its limbs curl round the walls. It is the only room on the street up off the ground: dark words on silvered planks against the sky, the leaves gold, rust and crimson, and nothing in it moves. Ben, a tiny black dog, lives there too, and one song plays on repeat: Alison Krauss & Union Station’s Let Me Touch You For Awhile, written by Robert Lee Castleman, 3:23 and round again until you stop it. Nothing plays until you press. Jess founded and runs GROVE, mentoring, interest groups and BEING ME for Autistic young people, by Autistic adults, and the room links to it. Between the pitches, and belonging to none of them: a pond with swing seats on its bank and a playground for pets, at Helen’s ask, drawn on the campgrounds’ board in the field’s own inks, with pebble paths from it to the yurt’s door, the tree house’s ladder and on across the field to the Solarpunk Hermitage. Every pitch stays where it is. Every home on the campgrounds now names its neighbours: the Faery Yurt, the Bough House and the Solarpunk Hermitage each carry a line linking the others, by name and by whose they are. A new tool writes it from the campgrounds’ board, so when somebody new pitches a home, every neighbour’s line takes them in the next time the street is checked, and nobody keeps the list by hand. It is a street convention, so it wears each room’s own ink. On the board, the tree house’s sign is the fifth light: the last sun, still on the top of the tree after it has left the field. A job marker (an acorn), a share card, a fractal, the map and Now Playing, and Merienda and Overlock, typefaces new to the street. Small screens and print move along to §118 and §119 of the stylesheet.

item.title: Every entry on this page stands on its own again
item.description: One entry here left its list open: the 2026-10-14 entry for the Faery Yurt’s welcome. Every entry below it, 252 of them, was nested inside that one list, and anything that reads the page’s structure saw one long entry. The Knowledge System’s copy of this page lost most of its entries that way. The list is closed now. The tool that builds the feed now refuses an entry whose lists do not close, and names it, so the next one is stopped before it is published rather than found three days after.

item.title: Wand & Rabbit, the jacket as a sticker, and downloads from Profile
item.description: A patch in The Chappell: Wand & Rabbit, dropped at the foot of the Magician’s Cut’s arch. It is shaped like one of the chapel’s pointed arches, in gold leaf on the nave’s indigo, and lettered in Monoton, the chapel’s own face. Your whole battle jacket is a sticker now. Sticker on the radio shows it first among your patches, and sending it sends a copy of which patches are on it as it is, with their names under it for everybody. Picking up another patch later does not change a jacket already sent. The privacy page says so. Download, in Profile, saves a picture of each of your avatars, pets and badges, of your battle jacket, and of every patch on it one at a time. The PNG is made in your browser from the drawing on your screen, with the typefaces its words are set in put inside it, and goes nowhere but your own device. The CB guide has the buttons.

item.title: Nick Walker’s card in the Reading Room
item.description: Nick Walker has a card in the catalogue’s Neurodivergence drawer, at Helen’s ask: Neuroqueer Heresies, and the four Spoon Knife anthologies Walker co-edited, each with its co-editors named. None has a page of its own on Wikipedia yet, so the titles are not doors; Walker’s spine on the Neurodivergence shelf still opens the Wikipedia page.

item.title: Different Bodies on Nick Totton’s card
item.description: Nick Totton’s card in the Reading Room’s catalogue has his second book, at Helen’s ask: Different Bodies: Deconstructing Normality (PCCS Books, 2023), after Wild Therapy. It has no page of its own on Wikipedia yet, so its title is not a door.

item.title: A card catalogue in the Reading Room, and three more authors
item.description: The Reading Room has a card catalogue, at Helen’s ask to list the titles behind some of her spines: a drawer for each case under the bookcases, with a card for each author that pulls out to show the books. Every title with a page of its own on Wikipedia is a door to it. The spines stay one author each, as she designed them, and nothing moves unless somebody opens a card. The cards so far: Joy Harjo and Sylvia Plath in Poetry; Haruki Murakami and Virginia Woolf in Novels; Henri Bergson, Gilles Deleuze and Félix Guattari together and each alone, Mark Fisher, Elizabeth Freeman, Donna Haraway, Erin Manning, Maurice Merleau-Ponty, José Esteban Muñoz and Spinoza in Philosophy; Nick Totton and Anna Lowenhaupt Tsing in Earth & Kin; bell hooks and Leah Lakshmi Piepzna-Samarasinha in Liberation & Rest; Robert Chapman and Steve Silberman in Neurodivergence. Three more spines: Joy Harjo on Poetry, for How We Became Human, and Elizabeth Freeman, for Time Binds, and José Esteban Muñoz, for Cruising Utopia, on Philosophy. Each opens its author’s page on Wikipedia, and the spine colours after each move along one, as before.

item.title: Robert Chapman and Nick Totton in the Reading Room
item.description: Two more authors on Helen’s shelves, at her ask: Robert Chapman, for Empire of Normality, on the Neurodivergence case, and Nick Totton, for Wild Therapy, on Earth & Kin. Chapman’s spine opens their page on Wikipedia, and Totton’s opens his own site, since Wikipedia has no page for him. The other books she named were already shelved by their authors: Leah Lakshmi Piepzna-Samarasinha (Care Work) and bell hooks (All About Love) on Liberation & Rest, Donna Haraway (Staying with the Trouble) on Philosophy, and Steve Silberman (NeuroTribes) on Neurodivergence. The shelves still go alphabetically by surname, so the spine colours after each new book move along one, to keep the six colours turning in order.

item.title: The yurt’s fire glows, and you can get more logs
item.description: The stove in the Faery Yurt glows now, at Helen’s ask: a warm light round it from the start, which spreads and brightens with every log you pop on the fire. It changes only when somebody presses, and nothing flickers or flashes. A Get more logs button fills the basket again whenever you like, and the fire keeps burning as it was. Pop a log on with an empty basket and the stove says to get more.

item.title: Pop a log on the fire in the yurt
item.description: The logs in the Faery Yurt’s basket go on the fire now, at Helen’s ask: press Pop a log on the fire under the stove, or press a log in the basket, and it lifts across into the stove’s window and the fire burns brighter, its flame taller, its heart lit and its glow warm on the floor. When the basket is empty the button fills it again and the fire settles back down. The basket says it in Helen’s words: pop one on the fire and warm yourself up! What happened is said in words under the button at every setting of the dial; at Gentle a log moves straight to the fire rather than flying there. Nothing flashes, nothing is counted, and nothing is kept, so the basket is full again next time.

item.title: The Moon Spoon Pebbling Pot in the yurt
item.description: The Faery Yurt has a window beside the stove and the stump now, called the Moon Spoon Pebbling Pot, at Helen’s ask, with her moon stone and her moon spoon drawn on the sill among red toadstools and ivy. The stone’s purple is the one new colour in her room, and it carries no word. Through the window plays Moon Spoon, Vi Hart’s video, from her own Vimeo, 6:30, credited to her on the window and in the liner notes. The moon spoon is Vi Hart’s idea. Nothing plays until you press, and the player is asked not to track the visit. Vimeo is a new service on the street, so the security header and the privacy page name it. Helen’s own photographs lie on the sill: her moon spoon with flowers she gathered in the local woods, the flowers on the table and in a basket, and her faery garden with a spoon hidden in the undergrowth. Each is recorded with the others, with no camera data kept and nothing done to the picture. And the log basket says it in Helen’s words now: free to take if you want, all yours! Enjoy!

item.title: A wood stove and a log basket in the yurt, and a hollow stump by the door
item.description: The basket to take a pebble from is a log basket now, at Helen’s ask, beside a little wood stove with its flue up through the crown, a fire in its window and a kettle on top, the way a yurt is really heated. It takes the place of the picnic hamper. The stove glows the candles’ own gold, so nothing in her room changes colour, and nothing in it moves. And the bowl to leave one in sits in a hollow tree stump, a carved wooden bowl in its hollow top, with ivy climbing its sides, red toadstools round its foot and a faery door in it, a post box for pebbles. There are toadstools and ivy round the stove and the log basket too, in a toadstool red that is new to her room, at her ask. The pebbles tool lets any room with a bowl name its own basket and bowl and draw them now. The Solarpunk Hermitage’s are just as they were.

item.title: Fantasy Fancy Dress, through the curtain at the back of the Dress-Up Den
item.description: A new shop behind the Dopamine Dress-Up Den, at Helen’s ask, with her name on the sign: Fantasy Fancy Dress. Faery wings from dragonfly to great faery wings, cat, fox, bunny, bear and mouse ears, tails, paws, bead necklaces, chunky beads, a pendant and a velvet choker, rings, bead bracelets and bangles, a onesie, and tiger, bear, dragon and unicorn suits. Every piece says how it feels and how it goes on and comes off, and comes in every print and colourway the Dress-Up Den has, all black included. Everything in it is worn by a bodymind, Helen’s call, because a tail or a pair of ears needs somebody to wear it. Bring your bodymind through from the Dress-Up Den and it is drawn there wearing whatever you pick; with nobody brought through, the shop draws somebody at random, a different somebody each time, so no body is the one it starts from. Take it back through and the Dress-Up Den keeps it as an avatar when you press Keep, wings and all. Nothing in the shop is kept or sent. The pieces go wherever your bodymind goes. They are drawn in the same file as every avatar on the street, on its feet or sitting down: wings fold flat for sitting back in a chair, a tail lies to one side, and short tails sit at the side of the seat where you can see them. The CB’s server and the page both refuse them on the Dress-Up Den’s stand. The room is lit only from behind, through lengths of sheer stuff in rose, mint, gold and lilac hanging from the ceiling, with the stock on the rail dark against the light and every word on the dark in front. A job marker lies on its floor, and the guild has posted the job.

item.title: The About page answers the questions people ask
item.description: Questions people ask, in Ryan Boren’s answers: what Stimpunks is and where the street fits in, how it started, why it looks like the old web and what AI makes possible, what the technology does for lived experience, what we hope and worry about with AI, and where to start. The answer about outside services names them: Netlify for hosting, Jitsi on 8x8 for calls, YouTube for most films, and Spotify, Apple Music and TIDAL for music, with a link to How the site runs, which lists every one. How the site runs had left TIDAL off its list of outside services since the records in Words, Bud, Beats started using it on 2026-10-10. It is on the list now.

item.title: What’s this all about? A page for anybody who does not get it yet
item.description: The street has an About page, for anybody who has been shown it and says they do not get it: what it is, what to do here, why a street, and a thirty-second film. The front page links it under the tagline, and so does the line at the foot of every page. The film was written as code by Claude in Claude Motion and exported to video. Its doors are the front page’s own, in their rooms’ own colours and lettered in their rooms’ own typefaces, from this site’s font files. It is silent, it plays only when you press play, and everything it shows is written out underneath it. It is the first film this site serves itself rather than from somebody else’s channel. How it’s made says so, and the liner notes credit every face in it.

item.title: The yurt’s soundtrack is a record case
item.description: A music library instead of a list of blocks, at Helen’s ask: the yarn’s rack is an arched case in the same design as her bookcases, with every song an LP sleeve standing on a plank, in one of her six spine colours with the disc peeking out. The sleeve is the press: it takes the record out, puts it on the phonograph and plays it, and says how long the record runs before you press. A small line under each sleeve still plays the song where it stands. The Reading Room goes gothic romance, at Helen’s ask: a brass chandelier over the scene, a candelabra either side of the hearth, seven candles in sconces along the wall above the bookcases, and ravens, one on the mantel looking at the fire, one at each end of the sconces and three perched on the arches. Every one is a drawing, and not one flame flickers. The Reading Room’s shelf note reads, in her words, that more are arriving as she remembers what she has read and loved and lent.

item.title: The yurt’s bookcases move into a Reading Room of their own
item.description: A new room behind the Faery Yurt, at Helen’s ask, because the bookcases had outgrown her page: The Reading Room, through the bookcase door where the shelves stood. Every one of her bookcases is in there now, every spine still a door to its author’s page, with a fire in a pointed stone hearth, a sofa, two chairs, candles in brass sconces on claret walls, and the gothic academia she asked for. Nothing in it flickers, and nothing moves at any setting unless you press Join the faeries or Grow a garden, which are in there as well as in the yurt. The yarn’s rack is a shelf of records now, at Helen’s ask: every song a sleeve in one of her six spine colours with the disc peeking out, standing on its own plank, and the press under it puts it on the phonograph as before. The yurt keeps its art gallery under the staircase, and where the bookshelf was there is the door. The yurt’s sign on the campgrounds board says a reading room of old books now rather than a plank shelf.

item.title: Sixty-three more books on the yurt’s shelves, and a ninth case
item.description: A hundred and thirty-five books now, at Helen’s ask, every one she has read, shelved alphabetically where it belongs and opening its author’s Wikipedia page like the rest. Poetry gains Keats, Tennyson, Christina Rossetti, Hopkins, Rilke, Rumi, Dylan Thomas, Carol Ann Duffy, Ocean Vuong, Kae Tempest and Kate Fox; Novels gains Angela Carter, Toni Morrison, Jean Rhys, Kazuo Ishiguro, Octavia E. Butler, Kafka and Dostoevsky; Philosophy gains Bachelard, Merleau-Ponty, Simone Weil, Hannah Arendt, Iris Murdoch, Donna Haraway, Jane Bennett, Timothy Morton, Byung-Chul Han, Nietzsche, Camus, and two Posthuman Press anthologies edited by Ombre Tarragnat, Divergences: An Anthology of Neurodissident Worlds and Entanglements: An Anthology of Posthuman Tales, each a spine named for the book; Liberation & Rest gains Eli Clare, Alice Wong, Leah Lakshmi Piepzna-Samarasinha, Johanna Hedva, Sunaura Taylor, Mia Mingus, Angela Davis, Mariame Kaba, Paulo Freire and Rebecca Solnit; and Earth & Kin gains Nan Shepherd, Rachel Carson, Annie Dillard, David Abram, Roger Deakin, Robert Macfarlane, Kathleen Jamie, Suzanne Simard and Emergence Magazine. A ninth case, Neurodivergence: Steve Silberman’s NeuroTribes and Nick Walker, moved across from Liberation & Rest, with Dinah Murray, Damian Milton, Luke Beardon, Devon Price, Pete Wharmby, Fern Brady, Katherine May, Sara Gibbs, Chloé Hayden, M. Remi Yergeau’s Authoring Autism, David Gray-Hammond, and Helen’s own books. Two cases of Helen’s own, at her ask, built from her publications page at More Realms: Helen’s Shelf, her books, chapters, review, translation, the work that carries her endorsement and the work that cites or features hers, and Autistic Realms Resources, her ebooks, webinar companions, workbooks and training packs. Each spine carries a short title and opens the page her list gives for it; work still without a publisher or an address is left off until it has one. Seven spines open somewhere other than Wikipedia, because Wikipedia has no article for them: Kate Fox’s, Pete Wharmby’s and Emergence Magazine’s open their own sites, the two anthologies open their pages at Posthuman Press, David Gray-Hammond’s (his books, at NeuroHub Community’s book store, where his old Emergent Divergence address now goes) and Helen’s (Autistic Realms). Astrida Neimanis’s stays plain.

item.title: Faeries with a capital F, and a fuller garden round the words
item.description: Faeries is spelt with a capital F wherever a visitor reads it in the Faery Yurt, the Reading Room and the Music Room, at Helen’s ask: on the switch, in the line under it, in what the switch says when pressed, and in the yurt’s own tagline. Grow a garden grows more: more small flowers in many colours and more toadstools along every vine, more vines across the top and the foot, and more mushrooms coming up out of the bottom, so the open ground all round the words fills in. It still never grows over a word, and it still takes its time.
